component_details.description: An outline of the overall goal that the NS seeks to achieve in its disaster and crisis response operations. The goal considers: context analysis, ongoing/regular all-hazards risk assessments: it may define the target proportion of affected population that will be reached, and a definition of the areas/sectors where a NS will usually respond during an emergency.

component_responses.notes: Planned/ goal after the completion of PER

component_details.title: DRM Policy
component_details.description: Reflects the NS mission, RCRC principles and mandate. It acknowledges other relevant NS policies, and aligns with the government policy (where applicable), incorporating the general rules that the NS will obey in order to achieve something (i.e mandate, strategy, etc.)

component_responses.notes: JRC DM policy does not exist, IFRC policy is adopted

component_details.title: DRM Laws, Advocacy and Dissemination
component_details.description: Designed to support the NS in improving legal preparedness for disasters and crisis and to promote the use of the IDRL Guidelines in order to reduce human vulnerability.

component_responses.notes: Official meetings were held in April 2021 and others are planned with the authorities and relevant stakeholders for the purpose of legistlating the IDRL & auxiliary role and including it in the national contingency plan

component_details.title: Quality and accountability
component_details.description: Describes the essential elements of principled, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian action. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_responses.notes: Quality and accountability measures are a high matter of interest that needs to be enhanced and documented in a formal non-customary practices

component_details.title: RC auxiliary role, Mandate and Law
component_details.description: A constitutional reference to the role of the NS in responding to disasters and crises, which may be legislated or included/ recognized in the National Response System.

component_responses.notes: Article 6 & 7 - Act of law No.3 for the year 1969 as amended

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_responses.notes: Surge team planned tp visit Hordan in order to conduct the context and risk assessment, six JRC staff were trainined on GIS in order to create maps and monitor potential hazards.

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_responses.notes: 8 different scenarios mentoned in the national contingency plan (each scenario is classifed by the likelihood)

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_responses.notes: Main objective of EOC once capacity is effeciently built

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes: Buisness Continuity Plan only addresses COVID-19 pandemic, high priority to be include all types of risks/threats

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_responses.notes: High priority

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_details.title: Coordination with local community level responders
component_details.description: Engagement with Community Disaster Response Teams (CDRTs), through training, coordination, and the development of community disaster preparedness and response plans.

component_responses.notes: BERCS does not have a formal documented procedure, but generally good communication flow exists between HQ and branches. Branch committee exists to coordinate with the branch staff, then this information goes to the HQ office. While the procedures are not documented they are followed consistently.

component_details.title: Cooperation with private sector
component_details.description: Mechanism that allows cooperation with private sector that often plays a strong role in response, particularly if there is impact on their staff and businesses. There is often a willingness to donate goods and services. Advance agreements help to expedite response actions.

component_responses.notes: NS ensures due diligence (background checks consistently applied) when selecting partners and accepting donations to mitigate image or reputational risks. NS ensures appropriate use of emblem and protects the organization's visual identity. NS has mechanisms in place to train and use volunteers from corporate partners (notable is engagement with the University of eSwatini as an outside actor to the movement).

component_details.title: Coordination with External Agencies and NGOs
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and collaboration with Non-Governmental Organization (NGO), both local and international NGOs, civil society organizations (CSOs) and United Nations agencies in country.

component_responses.notes: BERCS is very evidently an active member of the humanitarian community (UN, NGO) for coordination and efficiency of response.   The IASC mandated cluster system has not been initiated in-country as is not widely known about. Key personnel are aware of the IFRC’s role in the Shelter Cluster.   Knowledge of UN-led appeal and strategic processes is centred around the Office of the Secretary General as well as the technical officers. BERCS is an implementer for UN with key emergency response agreements with UN/NGO partners in-country, formalized and shared between branches and headquarters.

component_details.title: Civil Military Relations
component_details.description: Dialogue and interaction with military actors, essential to protect and promote humanitarian principles, avoid competition, minimize inconsistency and, when appropriate, pursue common goals.

component_responses.notes: Coordination arrangements exist with military and adhere to Fundamental Principles and International Humanitarian Law (IHL). BERCS applies the Movement guidance on the Movement and Military bodies when and where relevant.   BERCS is an active member of the in-country IHL committee. The NS promotes Fundamental Principles and appropriate use of the Movement emblems.  During covid NS was allowed to continue with all project activities for covid-related projects, and other projects to ensure continuity. Permission cards/letters in use to allow movement of RC staff and volunteers.

component_details.title: Coordination with Movement
component_details.description: Mechanisms that facilitate the coordination with ICRC, IFRC, and PNS in-country.

component_responses.notes: Coordination and cooperation adhere to SMCC principles. Close links with the CCST Southern Africa and in-country coordination mechanisms are established with Movement partners to share information. Information sharing with neighbouring NS has happened but is not regarded as systematic

component_details.title: Coordination with authorities
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and cooperation with local and national authorities. It is connected to the NS auxiliary role for humanitarian assistance.

component_responses.notes: BERCS has exemplary coordination practice with the authorities.

component_details.title: Staff and volunteer management
component_details.description: Well-functioning staff and volunteer management systems and practices allow for effective recruitment, supervision, support and encouragement of staff and volunteers.

component_responses.notes: Responders are deployed and equipped according to ToRs. Mandatory training on quality and accountability standards (Sphere, Code of Conduct, etc...) is in place pre-deployment and are selected from an accessible, up-to-date database of responder’s contacts and capacities at branch and HQ level (not yet digitised). Procedures exist to activate, deploy and manage branch and national response teams and all have official updated ID recognised by authorities and appropriate visibility items.   There is space to recruit volunteers from relevant sectors to maintain a diverse workforce and needs to develop expedited procedures to incorporate spontaneous volunteers during emergencies which meet minimum screening procedures and comply with its volunteer in emergency policy.   HR Policy supports recognition of volunteers however formal procedures not in place (appreciation certificates have been given out at regional level). Procedures to manage scale need to be documented and improved. Rotation system in place, however procedures not formally documented, rotation and retention mentioned in the HR policy however could be better defined.   The CoC is not physically signed by all staff but contract is signed and it's included in HR policy. Volunteers usually sign something that includes this.

component_details.title: Safety and security management
component_details.description: Addresses policy and procedures to ensure the safety of staff and volunteers. This include awareness, effective recruitment, training and management processes in place to ensure that personnel are capable of undertaking the roles demanded of them (from NS operational, management and leaders) according to the Stay Safe (IFRC) and Safer Access (ICRC). Based on safer access framework, including concepts of access, perception, identification and acceptance, and protection and violence prevention.

component_responses.notes: Many of the principles of SAF are applied in the NS approach but it is not systematically applied. Safety and security referenced in staff/ volunteer policies and updates are given to staff and volunteers (in particular BERCS has ensured the most up to date information on covid risk has been made available to all staff and volunteers).   Stay Safe training is completed by staff, however gaps exist with additional training and ensuring that staff and volunteers know safety and security rules beyond covid. There is not yet a system in place for staff and volunteers to report safety and security risks and incidents.

component_details.title: Communication in emergencies
component_details.description: Incorporates a system of public messaging to enable the NS to share timely, accurate information before, during, and after a disaster or crisis.

component_responses.notes: Communications focal points are identified and trained at headquarters but remain to be put in place at branch level, standard templates for communication are not yet available. The SG is the official spokesperson designated in an emergency. NS uses public and social media to draw attention to unmet needs, and rights of affected people, however does not yet have a social networking policy and guidelines for staff and volunteer conduct.  There is no external communication plan, however regular comms with communities is something that the NS is familiar with (there are processes in place that are well known among the team and staff).    Key messages and public awareness messages in an emergency are developed and shared with staff regularly. NS has capacity to track negative media and social media and react accordingly. NS coordinates with IFRC/ICRC on joint communication (SMCC).  BERCS has capacity to generate evidence-based results/messages to advocate to targeted audiences, i.e. decision makers and communities.

component_details.title: Operations Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Learning
component_details.description: The PMERL is designed to implement a results-based planning, monitoring and evaluation system that provides an evidence base of NS performance, including relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, sustainability and impact. A reliable and trusted organization is accountable, providing transparent and timely information and building systems to strengthen data collection and reporting. It is data-driven, analytical and results-based.

component_responses.notes: The NS does not have a dedicated PMER function, however there is an M&E function attached to projects as standard. NS refers to lessons learned from previous operations and revises plans according to developing need on the ground. NS submits reports as expected and according to agreements with partners. There is consistent information sharing and reporting with IFRC. Reporting on response includes sharing of information to all partners on Movement-wide contributions to the operation.

component_details.title: Finance and Admin policy and emergency procedures
component_details.description: Overall budgeting, accounting, treasury, assets, financial reporting and financial services operations. it also includes the efficient delivery , cost effective and timely services to the NS. Pre-approved, auditable, expedited procedures that allow for flexibility during a disaster/crisis. These must meet transparency, oversight and accountability standards. Procedures may include faster approval processes, fewer signatures, different authority levels. The Emergency Procedures are activated for a specific period of time.

component_responses.notes: NS has a Finance Policy in place, in addition to automated accounting and financial reporting systems. Emergency SOPs are included within the Finance Policy.   NS has systems and procedures in place for control and oversight to prevent acts of fraud and/or corruption which can be applied during an emergency. Relevant admin finance staff and operation managers are familiar with existing emergency related MoUs or agreements for compliance.  There are no EOC SOPs in place to align with the activation of Finance and Admin emergency procedures.

component_details.title: Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
component_details.description: Refers to technologies that provide access to information through telecommunications. This includes the Internet, wireless networks, mobile phones, radios and other communication mediums.

component_responses.notes: NS has a strong online presence and social media platform (i.e. WhatsApp, Viber, Line, Facebook etc.) which is used for emergency communication and messaging. Contact details for all staff are held by the team, given the relatively small size of the NS this functions well, and contact cards are not in use.   NS does not provide mobile phones or SIM cards, nor does it provide recharging equipment, however it does provide cards/loads to facilitate communications. The NS does not have radio capacity, satellite phone capacity, or trained IT support focal points.   NS has portable generators to ensure continuity of operations at key HQ and branch locations, however backup generators are not available where needed.

component_details.title: Resource Mobilisation
component_details.description: A documented strategy for raising domestic funds from the government, private sector, general public and other in-country actors to support the national society’s response. This would include allocation of responsibilities, practical mechanisms for accepting funds and for being accountable on funds.

component_responses.notes: Key staff are familiar with resource mobilisation options for humanitarian operations and a response mobilisation strategy (not yet based on the response strategy until available), available funds and the scale of need is in final draft form.   The National Resource Mobilisation Strategy is sufficient for both HQ and branches given the size of the country. NS has agreements and mechanisms for collaboration and fundraising with the private sector.  Mobilisation of resources for preparedness remains to be addressed as does the establishment of a national emergency fund, the recruitment of a resource mobilisation focal point, and supporting pre-disaster agreements. NBERCS does not have a pre-defined list of acceptable in-kind donations or tracking system.

NS has a dedicated function/unit to carry out and coordinate all logistics activities, i.e. procurement, stock management and warehousing, transport and fleet. JDs are available for all staff and have received training for their functions. Pre-positioned items meet the need on the ground.   There has not yet been an analysis of optimal supply chain options (e.g. prepositioned relief items, pre-existing agreements with suppliers, environmental impact) in terms of cost, speed and reliability. Volunteers are not trained to support surge logistics functions.  NS coordinates their stock and equipment with other key stakeholders in-country (notably NDMA) and adheres to Movement standards for procured goods, however standards may not be met when using donations.   No specific documented SOP for the management of in-kind donations exists (only medical supplies managed according to written standards); stock books in place for oversight; items classified and stored in warehouse and then distributed according to need.   There is no documented, expedited procedure in existence for branches to request additional relief items and/or equipment for early action and immediate response. The NS is aware of procedures for out-of-country donations; however any out-of-country is liable to tax according to current agreement.  NS has trained personnel for procurement along with documented and approved emergency procurement procedures which can be used in emergency settings.   Supplier database includes the option to blacklist suppliers who are in breach of Code of Conduct or are not performing as per agreement, but NS does not have up-to-date pre-agreements with suppliers to be able to immediately access supplies and/or services necessary for humanitarian response.  NS has a fleet manual including road safety and security, vehicle management and maintenance, insurance and registration, and staff are familiar with content however it is noted as requiring improvement.   All NS vehicles meet safety standards however numbers of vehicles are not sufficient for disaster response. The NS is yet to map in-country resources to rent or borrow cars.   Vehicles in place are covered by insurance, drivers are tested at recruitment stage only, but all have valid driver’s licences (regular testing is required) and are trained in First Aid and Safer Access (defensive driving is pending).  NS does not yet have an approved warehouse and stock management manual with standard forms and templates, however BERCS has a secure, dedicated, and appropriate space with 24/7 access to receive, store and dispatch relief supplies and response equipment. NS shares storage space with NDMA (owned, rented, or shared with other organisations) near high-risk communities, accessible during disasters.

component_details.title: RC auxiliary role, Mandate and Law
component_details.description: A constitutional reference to the role of the NS in responding to disasters and crises, which may be legislated or included/ recognized in the National Response System.

component_responses.notes: The NS role, mandate and law is clear and defined within the Act. The NS engages in IHL advocacy by engaging with relevant Government Authorities, Members of Parliament, and Public Security Management bodies, and has a place on the IHL Committee in country. NS action in country is directed from Ministries in accordance with Mandate.

component_details.title: DRM Strategy
component_details.description: An outline of the overall goal that the NS seeks to achieve in its disaster and crisis response operations. The goal considers: context analysis, ongoing/regular all-hazards risk assessments: it may define the target proportion of affected population that will be reached, and a definition of the areas/sectors where a NS will usually respond during an emergency.

component_responses.notes: There is a (near-final) draft of the NS Organizational strategy (2021 - 2024) which outlines strategic direction, and provides information on country context, and strategics goals. Draft shows clear engagement and consideration of technical sectors. DRM objectives are clearly outlined within the document. Some improvements could be made specifically related to the further development of a DRM strategy in order to outline hazard/risk assessment and target population that will be reached.

component_details.title: DRM Policy
component_details.description: Reflects the NS mission, RCRC principles and mandate. It acknowledges other relevant NS policies, and aligns with the government policy (where applicable), incorporating the general rules that the NS will obey in order to achieve something (i.e mandate, strategy, etc.)

component_responses.notes: The NS does not currently have DRM Policy or similar document to guide related action.

component_details.title: DRM Laws, Advocacy and Dissemination
component_details.description: Designed to support the NS in improving legal preparedness for disasters and crisis and to promote the use of the IDRL Guidelines in order to reduce human vulnerability.

component_responses.notes: While staff have been trained in IDRL and IHL, there is no IDRL humanitarian diplomacy plan in place. The NS is aware of the legal facilities however does not have standing exemptions (some projects qualify for exemptions depending on the source of funding)

component_details.title: Quality and accountability
component_details.description: Describes the essential elements of principled, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian action. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_responses.notes: The NS presents good examples of community engagement which informs projects development and design, as well as having functioning processes in place relating to community feedback mechanisms. While there are good processes in place there is room for improvement. Designated CEA focal persons can be identified and trained in all branches (currently only some branches have this in place). At the time of the assessment, a PSEA training is planned.   The NS is aware of and uses the CHS and Sphere standards in much of its work, e.g. community engagement and feedback mechanism, engaging in social protection issues, project technical specifications. While good examples have been shared, the application of this could be more systematic.   The NS is cognizant of social, economic, and environmental challenges and includes this in plans to the best of its ability, and is consistent in addressing standards for protection, gender, and inclusion in project design.

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes: The NS does not have an up-to-date business continuity plan in place, however it is clear that actions are taken to enable the NS to remain functional during times of stress (e.g. during COVID BERCS remained operational, adjusted to changing levels of staff availability, and applied required IPC controls).   BERCS has repurposed funds for COVID response operation from on-going projects.

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_responses.notes: SOPs are currently in development and thus not yet widely disseminated as awaiting final approval. The SOPs include early warning, early action.

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_responses.notes: Response and recovery planning interventions sit within the overall DM function, however are reactive to needs as they arise rather than being based on an overall organizational response plan which reflects in-country hazards and risk.   The NS does have processes to review and update plans once operational.   BERCS has contributed to the Cyclone Idai response in Mozambique, validating support and coordination with other NS in times of emergency.

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes: The NS has strong relationships and coordinates well with the various Government Ministries (this is evidenced throughout the assessment). This applies at National and local level with engagement in different technical sectors as mandated and required. Agreements with NDMA outline specifically how the NS and Gvt work together. There is no access to country-level databases of vulnerable populations. Agreements with public authorities to facilitate expedited import of humanitarian aid and visas happen on a case by case basis.   Improvements can be made with regard to engagement with the technical sector. While BERCS ensures service contracts adhere to the RCRC standards, the code of conduct remains to be signed alongside these contracts. There is one pre-existing standing contract with the mobile service provider for cash transfer activities.   Movement coordination agreements are known and available as needed, however the capacity mapping of Movement partners is not up to date.

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_responses.notes: The NS has a newly established relationship with the meteorological office and FbF project has just been initiated. There has been historic engagement within BERCS related to weather related challenges and monitoring of such. Work on this has been focused at community level and is currently project related. The NS is aware of the contextual challenges that exist through informal channels.   Currently there is no systematic, country-level hazard or risk mapping carried out by the NS. Where DRR committees have previously been established they no longer exist.   There is a sense of motivation to address this gap within the NS team and leadership.

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_responses.notes: Scenario planning and hazard and risk information is made readily available by the Government. The NS has strong relations and coordinates well with all sectoral and management authorities however does not have its own analysis nor scenario planning in place.

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_responses.notes: The NS is aware of the potential risk areas, and how to mitigate, however there is no risk framework in place. Anti-fraud and corruption policy is in place.   There is an acute awareness at senior level of the fact that risk areas are focused at project level, and not addressed more systematically.   The NS does not operate in an insecure context and thus analysis at this level has not yet taken place.

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_responses.notes: The NS Disaster Management Coordinator has this responsibility integrated into his role. Currently preparedness gaps are addressed through project interventions on an ad hoc basis and remedial action is taken accordingly, however there is no systematic mapping of preparedness needs against identified risk.   The NS has an organizational strategy which identifies key areas within DM, inclusive of preparedness.

BERCS implements food security projects as part of on-going operations and has clear mechanism to monitor the situation, both in-house and in coordination with others. Food security projects are supported through CTP, however cash training is recognized as an area which could be targeted for further training and improvement.   The challenge lies with not having a fully elaborated organizational response strategy, however some SOPs are in place.
Search and rescue is not currently part of a developed response strategy within BERCS

BERCS conducts regular awareness raising and public education on disasters or crises as relevant to the context at hand. There is clear engagement with communities to ensure active participation in  assessments and overall project design however the NS debates whether DP/DRR activities are genuinely ongoing. It has been noted as not being structured nor systematic.   Early warning systems are not yet active and will follow on with programme in initiation stages. CDRT training and strengthening will follow, but for now is not present within the functions of the NS.    It is noted that the NS ensures community assessment, planning and response are done in an inclusive, gender, diversity and conflict sensitive way

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_responses.notes: The DM Coordinator is the NS focal point identified for all sectors aside from Health, where the Health personnel represent the health sector. Both DM and health teams provide technical guidance and support.   Staff and volunteers are trained and kept up to date in the specific areas of intervention and services which is well outlined in the HR Policy.   It is noted that response materials and database is not up to date, and that some gaps exist in personnel.

With health clinics being a core service of the NS there is strong medical oversight for any intervention.   BERCS has a clearly evidenced relationship with communities which facilitates good information flow allowing the NS to engage the community in prevention and response actions. Rumours are managed efficiently with volunteers trained specifically for this task, supported by the communications team who develop materials and strategies for this purpose.    Safety procedures are in place for IPC (as mandated by the gvt) and clear systems are in place. The NS uses the guidance developed by the gvt during covid which is sufficient to meet expected standards. The operationalization of these standards at field level was in question by the NS teams.   The NS does not engage in SDB at this time and their role in isolation and  quarantine management has not been defined.

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_responses.notes: BERCS is in the very early stages of developing early warning systems supported by a FbF project. Initial efforts are ongoing to eventually meet the standards as set out by the benchmarks.

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_responses.notes: While the NS does not have a CBI preparedness plan, there is experience with CTP projects and a database of CBI trained and experienced staff and volunteers has been in place since 2016.   CBI procedures are in place however not formally documented.

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_responses.notes: NS has ENA standardised templates used for primary and secondary data collection and reporting supported by an emergency assessment team available to deploy in a timely manner.   BERCS contributes findings (disaggregated according to gender, age groups and others) to NDMA for nationally led emergency plans of action. NS assessment is not multi-sectoral and remains community level focussed for now. Templates currently do not consider secondary risk nor does the NS have the capacity to do this at the moment.

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_responses.notes: BERCS has a consistently established good relationship with the communities with whom they work, which is evident in the solid communication process followed in order to communicate selection criteria to the affected populations.   The NS has systems in place to protect data collected from the affected population. Standardised templates do not exist and are developed according to project need.   Clear processes are in place to support the NS in cross-checking affected populations' lists with community leaders, other agencies, authorities, etc… to verify inclusion/exclusion issues (basic data is shared only to take  protection of sensitive data into account)

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_responses.notes: The EOC function does not exist within the NS at this time, however close coordination with NDMA allows for streamlined response as required, including the provision of an additional space within which the NS can operate if needed. The NS present solid evidence of strategic decision-making in light of evolving operational gaps and needs.

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_responses.notes: BERCS has access to equipment to compile, visualise, and share information however does not have a system which facilitates easy sharing of critical information related to emergency response. Decisions are documented and filed.   BERCS does not have a standardised Situation Report format, nor are the teams familiar with IM templates, methodology, and procedures available from IFRC. Response plans are not currently in place within which collected information can be used.

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_responses.notes: BERCS does not tend to participate in NS drills or simulations, but participates in national-level drills, coordination, and preparedness activities.

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_responses.notes: Key staff within the NS are familiar with available IFRC/ICRC support, but does not have SOPs in place to coordinate or activate response.   The NS is aware of DREF and EPoA processes and has previously applied for DREFs. Bilateral support has been established in principle and international coordination is led by the SG and then delegated where relevant.

component_details.title: CHEMICAL, BIOLOGICAL, RADIOLOGICAL AND NUCLEAR (CBRN) EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS

component_responses.notes: The NS does not have a defined role and allied responsibilities in national, regional, and local authorities' emergency plans related to technological and biological hazards, nor is this sector reflected in any organisational document or procedures.

Livelihoods is included in response operations as standards (especially with regard to assessments - surveys and baselines) always have inclusion of this sector as standard. The NS has identified and documented main livelihoods zones and systems (agricultural and non-agricultural) and main market systems in coordination with the Government but not to the extent that the team was comfortable to confirm meeting the standards set out in the benchmark.   The focal person for Livelihoods is the DM coordinator. Staff and volunteers are trained in this area however capacity could be scaled up. BERCS coordinates with different MoA and other agencies in this area, however has yet to define its own livelihoods protection plans

NS has mechanisms for consultation with target population on the most appropriate shelter response solutions. Shelter supplies are centralised and appropriately located and accessible for the needs in-country. NFI kits are stored within the NS, with an agreement in place to access additional kits stored by the government at short notice when required. There are no pre-agreements in place with suppliers.   The NS does not have standard designs but ensures consultations on preferred techniques drive the overall response strategy. Volunteers are trained to use what the NS has stored.

component_details.title: MANAGEMENT OF DEAD BODIES TO FACILITATE THEIR IDENTIFICATION

component_responses.notes: BERCS is not part of the public authorities' management of dead bodies and identification system.

BERCS engages in RFL but not widely across the country. Communication service support is provided to refugees in-country and support is given to those no longer located with their families. This support was initially provided by ICRC however BERCS now maintains this role.

BERCS has a clear mandate in support of recovery efforts in country.  NS coordinates consistently with public authorities and humanitarian actors, participating in joint needs assessment and the national recovery and reconstruction planning (working closely with organisations that support household for longer-term shelter needs). The DM council is involved in this area in particular, on which BERCS has a seat.  The NS HR Policy is in place and could reflect the human resource requirements for this sector more effectively.

component_details.title: NS-specific areas of intervention
component_details.description: Sector-specific or services provided by the NS in case of emergencies, it is in line with the NS mandate and legislation in country. It includes Community Based DP/DRR, Evacuation, Health in Emergencies, Epidemic and Pandemic, First aid, WASH, Food security and Livelihoods, Search and rRescue, Shelter, Management of dead bodies, RFL, Transition to recovery, and CBRN preparedness.

component_responses.notes: The NS does not have a defined role within the mechanism for evacuation in-country, nor is this reflected in any NS documentation.
The NS does not have a response strategy currently, nor a CBDRR strategy, however First Aid volunteers are trained and equipped appropriately.

WASH training has been provided to NS teams however there is acknowledgement that the skills and equipment would not be sufficient for driving forward WASH sectoral response activities. BERCS engages in WASH consortiums in country but does not have the capacity in-house.

Some BERCS volunteers have participated in Basic First Aid training however not applicable to all volunteers. CBHFA volunteer training includes a session on proper reporting of suspect health events to branch staff and/or the Ministry of Health however CBHFS is not elaborated in contingency plans, assessments, or simulations at community level.

component_details.title: RC auxiliary role, Mandate and Law
component_details.description: A constitutional reference to the role of the NS in responding to disasters and crises, which may be legislated or included/ recognized in the National Response System.

component_details.title: DRM Strategy
component_details.description: An outline of the overall goal that the NS seeks to achieve in its disaster and crisis response operations. The goal considers: context analysis, ongoing/regular all-hazards risk assessments: it may define the target proportion of affected population that will be reached, and a definition of the areas/sectors where a NS will usually respond during an emergency.

component_details.title: DRM Policy
component_details.description: Reflects the NS mission, RCRC principles and mandate. It acknowledges other relevant NS policies, and aligns with the government policy (where applicable), incorporating the general rules that the NS will obey in order to achieve something (i.e mandate, strategy, etc.)

component_responses.notes: In procedure.

component_details.title: DRM Laws, Advocacy and Dissemination
component_details.description: Designed to support the NS in improving legal preparedness for disasters and crisis and to promote the use of the IDRL Guidelines in order to reduce human vulnerability.

component_details.title: Quality and accountability
component_details.description: Describes the essential elements of principled, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian action. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_responses.notes: It is needed that NS and the working group prioritise this issue, as well as to share the guidelines with all levels of the structure.

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_responses.notes: In procedure. It exists at the entity level for some phases as a part of DM (in RC FBiH in several branches, 10-15%) with certain weaknesses.

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_responses.notes: In procedure.

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_responses.notes: There is a legal framework related to local and entity cooperation (agreements with CP). It is necessary to include cross border cooperation of NS. Recommendation: mapping of capacities.

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_responses.notes: NS is not mandated for early warning of local communites.

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_responses.notes: There are certain activities and trained staff in certain locations.

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_details.title: Coordination with local community level responders
component_details.description: Engagement with Community Disaster Response Teams (CDRTs), through training, coordination, and the development of community disaster preparedness and response plans.

component_details.title: Cooperation with private sector
component_details.description: Mechanism that allows cooperation with private sector that often plays a strong role in response, particularly if there is impact on their staff and businesses. There is often a willingness to donate goods and services. Advance agreements help to expedite response actions.

component_details.title: Coordination with External Agencies and NGOs
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and collaboration with Non-Governmental Organization (NGO), both local and international NGOs, civil society organizations (CSOs) and United Nations agencies in country.

component_details.title: Civil Military Relations
component_details.description: Dialogue and interaction with military actors, essential to protect and promote humanitarian principles, avoid competition, minimize inconsistency and, when appropriate, pursue common goals.

component_responses.notes: Does not exist due to limitations in legislation. There are some mechanisms for civil-military cooperation.

component_details.title: Coordination with Movement
component_details.description: Mechanisms that facilitate the coordination with ICRC, IFRC, and PNS in-country.

component_details.title: Coordination with authorities
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and cooperation with local and national authorities. It is connected to the NS auxiliary role for humanitarian assistance.

component_details.title: Staff and volunteer management
component_details.description: Well-functioning staff and volunteer management systems and practices allow for effective recruitment, supervision, support and encouragement of staff and volunteers.

component_details.title: Safety and security management
component_details.description: Addresses policy and procedures to ensure the safety of staff and volunteers. This include awareness, effective recruitment, training and management processes in place to ensure that personnel are capable of undertaking the roles demanded of them (from NS operational, management and leaders) according to the Stay Safe (IFRC) and Safer Access (ICRC). Based on safer access framework, including concepts of access, perception, identification and acceptance, and protection and violence prevention.

component_responses.notes: Since 2016, the ICRC in cooperation with the IFRC and other partners actively works on development of the plan together with the NS.

component_details.title: Communication in emergencies
component_details.description: Incorporates a system of public messaging to enable the NS to share timely, accurate information before, during, and after a disaster or crisis.

component_details.title: Operations Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Learning
component_details.description: The PMERL is designed to implement a results-based planning, monitoring and evaluation system that provides an evidence base of NS performance, including relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, sustainability and impact. A reliable and trusted organization is accountable, providing transparent and timely information and building systems to strengthen data collection and reporting. It is data-driven, analytical and results-based.

component_details.title: Finance and Admin policy and emergency procedures
component_details.description: Overall budgeting, accounting, treasury, assets, financial reporting and financial services operations. it also includes the efficient delivery , cost effective and timely services to the NS. Pre-approved, auditable, expedited procedures that allow for flexibility during a disaster/crisis. These must meet transparency, oversight and accountability standards. Procedures may include faster approval processes, fewer signatures, different authority levels. The Emergency Procedures are activated for a specific period of time.

component_details.title: Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
component_details.description: Refers to technologies that provide access to information through telecommunications. This includes the Internet, wireless networks, mobile phones, radios and other communication mediums.

component_details.description: A documented strategy for raising domestic funds from the government, private sector, general public and other in-country actors to support the national society’s response. component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes: La CRC doit réactiver son plan de continuité des activités et le diffuser pour que les branches l'adaptent à leur contexte et leurs ressources de tout genre.

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_responses.notes: La CRC n’a pas de procédures d’opération standard, et par conséquent pas de procédures spéciales aux interventions d’urgence.

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_responses.notes: La SN n’a pas de plan d’intervention.

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes: Se fait plutot avec les parternaires du Mouvement et au besoin avec les autorité, mais pas en vu de planifier les roles et attentes de chaque parti de façon prédictive. La SN n'a pas d'accords formulés avec les fournisseurs pour couvrir tous les besoins possibles au début d'une réponse. Il est important de formaliser les accords et un mécanisme d'activation.

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_responses.notes: Vu que le Gouvernement s'occupe de la gestion des catastrophes, la SN n'a pas de mécanisme d'analyse et ne surveille pas les aléas, mais tache d'améliorer depuis quelques années sa préparation aux réponses en formant et recyclant les équipes des branches. Absence d'un système de suivi vu que les volontaires ne sont pas fidélisés et donc partent régulièrement chercher le pain quotidien, ayant pour conséquence de "recommencer le travail à zéro". Les moyens de communications, outils de travail, base de données et ressources financières limités ne facilitent pas cette activité, sans oublier la rotation du staff au niveau national qui a également un impact.

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_responses.notes: Les plans de contingences ne contiennent pas les éléments importants.

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_responses.notes: Se fait en pratique mais pas de documentation et le service y dedié n'est pas actif.

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_responses.notes: Un point focal a été identifié mais les plans et leurs budgets n’existent toujours pas

La SN a des volontaires formés dans quelques zones sur la sécurité économique et donc aussi à l'alimentation et aux moyens de subsistance, cependant un travail doit se faire pour avoir des capacités sur tout le territoire et pour mettre en place un système d'analyse et de surveillance et un plan d'action.
La CRC aide sur demande des autorités. Ce n'est pas fait de façon systématique et la technique manque.
Se fait plutôt pour les épidémies mais pas pour tous les risques.

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_responses.notes: La cartographie existe en quelque sorte pour les ressources humaines mais pas pour les autres ressources. Les inventaires ne se font pas et ne se mettent pas à jour de façon systématique. L’information existante n’est pas reliée aux besoins d’intervention initiaux.

Les besoins d’intervention multisectoriels, le rôle de la communauté et les protocoles de prévention des infections ne sont pas identifiés pour les différents scénarios d’épidémies, inclus ceux transfrontaliers. Les procédures de gérance des rumeurs et le rôle de la SN en cas d’isolement doivent être identifiées et vulgarisées.

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_responses.notes: La CRC n’a pas de mécanisme d’action précoce

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_responses.notes: Le mécanisme utilisé en cas d’intervention basée sur l’argent comptant se forme de zéro chaque fois que la SN en a besoin. Il n’y a pas de système et d’accords pre-établis qui faciliteraient le travail et le rendraient plus rapide.

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_responses.notes: Se fait par des équipes formées. Les modèles existent seulement au siège. Les branches utilisent les outils des partenaires pour pouvoir évaluer les besoins. Les données ne sont pas ventilées de façon détaillée.

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_responses.notes: Se fait mais nécessite beaucoup de renforcement et une institutionnalisation.

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_responses.notes: Le siège coordonne uniquement les réponses en internes selon le besoin. La SN suit le COU du Gouvernement. La NS gagnerait à avoir un véritable COU.

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_responses.notes: Les équipements de base ne sont pas à disposition du siège et des branches pour pouvoir faire le travail correctement.

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_responses.notes: Les recommandations ou rapports qui sortent des ateliers et des opérations ne sont pas utilisés pour améliorer la réponse.

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_responses.notes: La CRC requiert une bien meilleure prise en compte de ses capacités, et de son implication dans le déclenchement des interventions d’urgence, ainsi que la mise en place de procédures d’opération standard.

component_details.title: CHEMICAL, BIOLOGICAL, RADIOLOGICAL AND NUCLEAR (CBRN) EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS

component_responses.notes: Capacité inexistante.
Le point focal existe mais un système de mise en œuvre n’existe pas, ou existe dans très peu de branches.
Système de travail et capacité inexistants.

component_details.title: MANAGEMENT OF DEAD BODIES TO FACILITATE THEIR IDENTIFICATION

component_responses.notes: Fonctionne très bien.
La SN n’a pas de système et plan de transition vers le relèvement.

component_details.title: NS-specific areas of intervention
component_details.description: Sector-specific or services provided by the NS in case of emergencies, it is in line with the NS mandate and legislation in country. It includes Community Based DP/DRR, Evacuation, Health in Emergencies, Epidemic and Pandemic, First aid, WASH, Food security and Livelihoods, Search and rRescue, Shelter, Management of dead bodies, RFL, Transition to recovery, and CBRN preparedness.

component_responses.notes: La SN n'est pas formellement responsable de faire l'évacuation mais le fait quelque fois sous demande de la part des autorités.
Se fait assez bien, mais nécessite une procédure pour les réponses en cas d’épidémie, pour la prévention et le contrôle des infections.
Ce service est très faiblement développé.
Se fait dans le Nord, l’extrême Nord, l’Est et les branches du CP3. Nécessite d’être répliqué sur tout le territoire.

component_details.title: Coordination with local community level responders
component_details.description: Engagement with Community Disaster Response Teams (CDRTs), through training, coordination, and the development of community disaster preparedness and response plans.

component_responses.notes: Il n’existe pas d’équipes de réponse au niveau communautaire. Les branches comptent sur la relation avec les communauté pour collecter des informations.

component_details.title: Cooperation with private sector
component_details.description: Mechanism that allows cooperation with private sector that often plays a strong role in response, particularly if there is impact on their staff and businesses. There is often a willingness to donate goods and services. Advance agreements help to expedite response actions.

component_responses.notes: La CRC est de plus en plus sollicitée par le secteur privé, sans pour autant avoir un mécanisme de coopération qui augmenterait les capacité de réponse réduirait les risques sur la réputation.

component_details.title: Coordination with External Agencies and NGOs
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and collaboration with Non-Governmental Organization (NGO), both local and international NGOs, civil society organizations (CSOs) and United Nations agencies in country.

component_responses.notes: La coordination avec les agences externes et les ONG demande à être développée.

component_details.title: Civil Military Relations
component_details.description: Dialogue and interaction with military actors, essential to protect and promote humanitarian principles, avoid competition, minimize inconsistency and, when appropriate, pursue common goals.

component_responses.notes: Se fait de façon aléatoire sur le terrain. Restent à être systématisées.

component_details.title: Coordination with Movement
component_details.description: Mechanisms that facilitate the coordination with ICRC, IFRC, and PNS in-country.

component_responses.notes: La coordination avec le Mouvement est bonne et dynamique. Elle nécessite d'être institutionalisée à travers un mécanisme clair et connu des personnes clefs.

component_details.title: Coordination with authorities
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and cooperation with local and national authorities. It is connected to the NS auxiliary role for humanitarian assistance.

component_responses.notes: Le statut d’auxiliaire de la SN doit être bien défini avec les autorité pour qu’elle soit impliquée dans la planification et les réponses humanitaires.

component_details.title: Staff and volunteer management
component_details.description: Well-functioning staff and volunteer management systems and practices allow for effective recruitment, supervision, support and encouragement of staff and volunteers.

component_responses.notes: Très peu de pratiques existent.

component_details.title: Safety and security management
component_details.description: Addresses policy and procedures to ensure the safety of staff and volunteers. This include awareness, effective recruitment, training and management processes in place to ensure that personnel are capable of undertaking the roles demanded of them (from NS operational, management and leaders) according to the Stay Safe (IFRC) and Safer Access (ICRC). Based on safer access framework, including concepts of access, perception, identification and acceptance, and protection and violence prevention.

component_responses.notes: Système inexistant.

component_details.title: Communication in emergencies
component_details.description: Incorporates a system of public messaging to enable the NS to share timely, accurate information before, during, and after a disaster or crisis.

component_responses.notes: La SN possède les capacités et la compétence de faire fonctionner un tel système, mais la logistique et les procédures opérationnelles devant assurer la performance d’un tel système sont inexistantes.

component_details.title: Operations Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Learning
component_details.description: The PMERL is designed to implement a results-based planning, monitoring and evaluation system that provides an evidence base of NS performance, including relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, sustainability and impact. A reliable and trusted organization is accountable, providing transparent and timely information and building systems to strengthen data collection and reporting. It is data-driven, analytical and results-based.

component_responses.notes: Une personne rempli cette fonction pour un programme, quoique en urgence ceci ne se fait pas, et les capacités existantes ne sont pas suffisantes.

component_details.title: Finance and Admin policy and emergency procedures
component_details.description: Overall budgeting, accounting, treasury, assets, financial reporting and financial services operations. it also includes the efficient delivery , cost effective and timely services to the NS. Pre-approved, auditable, expedited procedures that allow for flexibility during a disaster/crisis. These must meet transparency, oversight and accountability standards. Procedures may include faster approval processes, fewer signatures, different authority levels. The Emergency Procedures are activated for a specific period of time.

component_responses.notes: Système inexistant.

component_details.title: Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
component_details.description: Refers to technologies that provide access to information through telecommunications. This includes the Internet, wireless networks, mobile phones, radios and other communication mediums.

component_details.title: Resource Mobilisation
component_details.description: A documented strategy for raising domestic funds from the government, private sector, general public and other in-country actors to support the national society’s response. This would include allocation of responsibilities, practical mechanisms for accepting funds and for being accountable on funds.

component_responses.notes: Système très faible; nécessite un appui technique pour mettre en place un mécanisme fonctionnel.

component_details.title: DRM Strategy
component_details.description: An outline of the overall goal that the NS seeks to achieve in its disaster and crisis response operations. The goal considers: context analysis, ongoing/regular all-hazards risk assessments: it may define the target proportion of affected population that will be reached, and a definition of the areas/sectors where a NS will usually respond during an emergency.

component_responses.notes: •	BRCS National Response Plan & Strategy (NRPS) is a comprehensive document.
