component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_responses.notes: Se pudo evidenciar que existe una descentralización del sistema de respuesta, en los niveles locales, regionales y nacionales, sin embargo en las entrevistas las personas manifestaron que no se observa que exista una desconcentración de recursos, en los planes se puede observar que existe una organizacion para la respuesta. Se pudo observar la Sociedad Nacional cuenta con procedimientos estandarizados, se observo que falta entrenamiento en el uso de procedimientos. A nivel de regional no se observo la división de roles y responsabilidades plasmadas en los planes entre la vicepresidencia regional y el presidente municipal del consejo de San Lorenzo invisibilizando el trabajo del consejo. Durante la simulación se observo que fue la vicepresidencia regional la que retomo la parte de toma de decisiones de las situaciones presentadas a nivel local. A nivel de filiales se pudo constatar que el personal no están familiarizados con el manual de procedimientos, en los planes regionales Se observan algunos procedimientos con sus diagramas de flujos  para funciones claves, también se pudo evidenciar que existen procedimientos operativos como el de atencion prehospitalaria, controladores de guardia,  vehículos de emergencias que cuentan con sus diagramas de flujo para su mas facil interpretacion Se puede evidenciar que aunque no existe un manual de funciones estos se ven reflejados en otros documentos como los planes de respuesta, los procedimientos  operativos y manual de funciones administrativas, se observo que las personas tienen autoridad formal para cada puesto, evitando así la duplicidad de esfuerzos.    Se debe realizar un proceso de entrenamiento para la apropiacion de los procedimientos a nivel nacional que permita el seguimiento de los mismos y la ´puesta en practica en el  momento de la emergencia.

Se pudo observar que las decisiones eran canalizadas hacia las áreas responsables, si se observaron algunas discrepancias en las decisiones tomadas, a nivel de filiales se observo que hubo poca priorización de las situaciones presentadas. Si cuentan con sistema de radio comunicación funcionando con cobertura a nivel nacional, no se evidencio que exista  teléfono satelital en el caso de que colapse las redes de radios, se constato que esta en proceso la firma del contrato con la empresa que esta encargadas del mantenimiento preventivo, en las filiales se observo poco uso de la redes de radios existentes(Base, movil y portatil) tienen 8 pares de frecuencias, con 8 repetidoras, ademas de un inventario que es manejado por el departamento de radios y se han realizado formaciones para el personal que opera los radios. Hay una Red de comunicadores, 30 personas distribuidas en todo el país. Las fuentes entrevistadas dijeron que hay una red de comunicadores de 30 en las cuatro regiones y que continuaran con las capacitaciones. También expresaron que las demás áreas y departamentos de la SN fortalecieran la coordinación con el área de comunicación, sobre todo en eventos programados.

component_details.title: Operations Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Learning
component_details.description: The PMERL is designed to implement a results-based planning, monitoring and evaluation system that provides an evidence base of NS performance, including relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, sustainability and impact. A reliable and trusted organization is accountable, providing transparent and timely information and building systems to strengthen data collection and reporting. It is data-driven, analytical and results-based.

component_responses.notes: Existe una unidad de monitoreo, evaluación y reportes que trabaja en coordinación con los equipos EDAN-PMER. También se observó que han tomado en cuenta los resultados y recomendaciones de otras evaluaciones, diagnósticos y operaciones de respuesta a emergencias. Se evidenció que la SN tiene una comunicación permanente con las instituciones del sistema  Se evidenció en la sede central el procesamiento de  información, reuniones para presentación de informes, existencia de unidades encargadas del manejo de información, sin embargo a nivel local se observo poco recurso humano con la capacidad para la administración de la información. Tambien se observo la utilización de herramientas  de visualización de datos para operativos como semana santa, semana Morazánica, entre otras.

component_details.title: Finance and Admin policy and emergency procedures
component_details.description: Overall budgeting, accounting, treasury, assets, financial reporting and financial services operations. it also includes the efficient delivery , cost effective and timely services to the NS. Pre-approved, auditable, expedited procedures that allow for flexibility during a disaster/crisis. These must meet transparency, oversight and accountability standards. Procedures may include faster approval processes, fewer signatures, different authority levels. The Emergency Procedures are activated for a specific period of time.

component_responses.notes: Se observo que se cuenta con un sistema de auditoria y finanzas que les permite tomar decisiones en el tiempo requerido, ademas de la existencia de una unidad de monitoreo y auditoria

component_details.title: Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
component_details.description: Refers to technologies that provide access to information through telecommunications. This includes the Internet, wireless networks, mobile phones, radios and other communication mediums.

component_responses.notes: Si cuentan con sistema de radio comunicación funcionando con cobertura a nivel nacional, no se evidencio que exista  teléfono satelital en el caso de que colapse las redes de radios, se constato que esta en proceso la firma del contrato con la empresa que esta encargadas del mantenimiento preventivo, en las filiales se observo poco uso de la redes de radios existentes(Base, movil y portatil) tienen 8 pares de frecuencias, con 8 repetidoras, ademas de un inventario que es manejado por el departamento de radios y se han realizado formaciones para el personal que opera los radios.

component_details.title: Resource Mobilisation
component_details.description: A documented strategy for raising domestic funds from the government, private sector, general public and other in-country actors to support the national society’s response. This would include allocation of responsibilities, practical mechanisms for accepting funds and for being accountable on funds.

component_responses.notes: EHay mecanismos pero no hay acuerdos firmados. Tienen 13 planes de negocio y un borrador de guía de responsabilidad social-empresarial. 2 consejos han logrado completar el plan y se les asignará capital. Durante las entrevistas de determinó que la SN cuenta con fondo de emergencias de USD$,5000.00, aproximadamente.

Durante las entrevistas se evidenció que la SN cuenta con procedimientos para compra, sin embargo no cuenta con una lista de proveedores para la adquisición de productos a la hora de una emergencia. Los niveles regionales y locales se adhieren a los procesos de compras implementados por la sede central. También se evidenció que aunque el plan de respuesta no incluye dentro de sus líneas de intervención centros de acopio, en la última emergencia el Consejo de Choluteca lo utilizaron como forma de adquisición de bienes.//Se evidenció que los vehículos cuentan con bitácoras para la realización de mantenimiento cada 5,000 km. Los conductores asignados son sometidos a prueba de manejo interna de la SN. No se cuenta con el mínimo de vehiculos necesarios para el desevolvimiento básico de los Consejos.//La SN cuenta con 5 almacenes, uno en el nivel nacional y uno por cada región. En las entrevistas se evidenció que cuentan con un sistema de control de  los artículos presposicionados en tres de los cinco almacenes, lo que les permite una listeza operacional en caso de un desastre.

component_details.title: RC auxiliary role, Mandate and Law
component_details.description: A constitutional reference to the role of the NS in responding to disasters and crises, which may be legislated or included/ recognized in the National Response System.

component_details.title: DRM Strategy
component_details.description: An outline of the overall goal that the NS seeks to achieve in its disaster and crisis response operations. The goal considers: context analysis, ongoing/regular all-hazards risk assessments: it may define the target proportion of affected population that will be reached, and a definition of the areas/sectors where a NS will usually respond during an emergency.

component_details.title: DRM Policy
component_details.description: Reflects the NS mission, RCRC principles and mandate. It acknowledges other relevant NS policies, and aligns with the government policy (where applicable), incorporating the general rules that the NS will obey in order to achieve something (i.e mandate, strategy, etc.)

component_details.title: DRM Laws, Advocacy and Dissemination
component_details.description: Designed to support the NS in improving legal preparedness for disasters and crisis and to promote the use of the IDRL Guidelines in order to reduce human vulnerability.

component_details.title: Quality and accountability
component_details.description: Describes the essential elements of principled, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian action. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_details.title: CHEMICAL, BIOLOGICAL, RADIOLOGICAL AND NUCLEAR (CBRN) EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS
MANAGEMENT OF DEAD BODIES TO FACILITATE THEIR IDENTIFICATION
NS-specific areas of intervention
component_details.description: Sector-specific or services provided by the NS in case of emergencies, it is in line with the NS mandate and legislation in country. It includes Community Based DP/DRR, Evacuation, Health in Emergencies, Epidemic and Pandemic, First aid, WASH, Food security and Livelihoods, Search and rRescue, Shelter, Management of dead bodies, RFL, Transition to recovery, and CBRN preparedness.

component_details.title: Coordination with local community level responders
component_details.description: Engagement with Community Disaster Response Teams (CDRTs), through training, coordination, and the development of community disaster preparedness and response plans.

component_details.title: Cooperation with private sector
component_details.description: Mechanism that allows cooperation with private sector that often plays a strong role in response, particularly if there is impact on their staff and businesses. There is often a willingness to donate goods and services. Advance agreements help to expedite response actions.

component_details.title: Coordination with External Agencies and NGOs
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and collaboration with Non-Governmental Organization (NGO), both local and international NGOs, civil society organizations (CSOs) and United Nations agencies in country.

component_details.title: Civil Military Relations
component_details.description: Dialogue and interaction with military actors, essential to protect and promote humanitarian principles, avoid competition, minimize inconsistency and, when appropriate, pursue common goals.

component_details.title: Coordination with Movement
component_details.description: Mechanisms that facilitate the coordination with ICRC, IFRC, and PNS in-country.

component_details.title: Coordination with authorities
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and cooperation with local and national authorities. It is connected to the NS auxiliary role for humanitarian assistance.

component_details.title: Staff and volunteer management
component_details.description: Well-functioning staff and volunteer management systems and practices allow for effective recruitment, supervision, support and encouragement of staff and volunteers.

component_details.title: Safety and security management
component_details.description: Addresses policy and procedures to ensure the safety of staff and volunteers. This include awareness, effective recruitment, training and management processes in place to ensure that personnel are capable of undertaking the roles demanded of them (from NS operational, management and leaders) according to the Stay Safe (IFRC) and Safer Access (ICRC). Based on safer access framework, including concepts of access, perception, identification and acceptance, and protection and violence prevention.

component_details.title: Communication in emergencies
component_details.description: Incorporates a system of public messaging to enable the NS to share timely, accurate information before, during, and after a disaster or crisis.

It includes Community Based DP/DRR, Evacuation, Health in Emergencies, Epidemic and Pandemic, First aid, WASH, Food security and Livelihoods, Search and rRescue, Shelter, Management of dead bodies, RFL, Transition to recovery, and CBRN preparedness.

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_details.title: Coordination with local community level responders
component_details.description: Engagement with Community Disaster Response Teams (CDRTs), through training, coordination, and the development of community disaster preparedness and response plans.

component_details.title: Cooperation with private sector
component_details.description: Mechanism that allows cooperation with private sector that often plays a strong role in response, particularly if there is impact on their staff and businesses. There is often a willingness to donate goods and services. Advance agreements help to expedite response actions.

component_details.title: Coordination with External Agencies and NGOs
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and collaboration with Non-Governmental Organization (NGO), both local and international NGOs, civil society organizations (CSOs) and United Nations agencies in country.

component_details.title: Civil Military Relations
component_details.description: Dialogue and interaction with military actors, essential to protect and promote humanitarian principles, avoid competition, minimize inconsistency and, when appropriate, pursue common goals.

component_details.title: Coordination with Movement
component_details.description: Mechanisms that facilitate the coordination with ICRC, IFRC, and PNS in-country.

component_details.title: Coordination with authorities
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and cooperation with local and national authorities. It is connected to the NS auxiliary role for humanitarian assistance.

component_details.title: Staff and volunteer management
component_details.description: Well-functioning staff and volunteer management systems and practices allow for effective recruitment, supervision, support and encouragement of staff and volunteers.

component_details.title: Safety and security management
component_details.description: Addresses policy and procedures to ensure the safety of staff and volunteers. This include awareness, effective recruitment, training and management processes in place to ensure that personnel are capable of undertaking the roles demanded of them (from NS operational, management and leaders) according to the Stay Safe (IFRC) and Safer Access (ICRC). Based on safer access framework, including concepts of access, perception, identification and acceptance, and protection and violence prevention.

component_details.title: Communication in emergencies
component_details.description: Incorporates a system of public messaging to enable the NS to share timely, accurate information before, during, and after a disaster or crisis.

component_details.title: Operations Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Learning
component_details.description: The PMERL is designed to implement a results-based planning, monitoring and evaluation system that provides an evidence base of NS performance, including relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, sustainability and impact. A reliable and trusted organization is accountable, providing transparent and timely information and building systems to strengthen data collection and reporting. It is data-driven, analytical and results-based.

component_details.title: Finance and Admin policy and emergency procedures
component_details.description: Overall budgeting, accounting, treasury, assets, financial reporting and financial services operations. it also includes the efficient delivery , cost effective and timely services to the NS. Pre-approved, auditable, expedited procedures that allow for flexibility during a disaster/crisis. These must meet transparency, oversight and accountability standards. Procedures may include faster approval processes, fewer signatures, different authority levels. The Emergency Procedures are activated for a specific period of time.

component_details.title: Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
component_details.description: Refers to technologies that provide access to information through telecommunications. This includes the Internet, wireless networks, mobile phones, radios and other communication mediums.

component_details.title: Resource Mobilisation
component_details.description: A documented strategy for raising domestic funds from the government, private sector, general public and other in-country actors to support the national society’s response. This would include allocation of responsibilities, practical mechanisms for accepting funds and for being accountable on funds.

component_details.title: DRM Strategy
component_details.description: An outline of the overall goal that the NS seeks to achieve in its disaster and crisis response operations. The goal considers: context analysis, ongoing/regular all-hazards risk assessments: it may define the target proportion of affected population that will be reached, and a definition of the areas/sectors where a NS will usually respond during an emergency.

component_details.title: DRM Policy
component_details.description: Reflects the NS mission, RCRC principles and mandate. It acknowledges other relevant NS policies, and aligns with the government policy (where applicable), incorporating the general rules that the NS will obey in order to achieve something (i.e mandate, strategy, etc.)

component_details.title: DRM Laws, Advocacy and Dissemination
component_details.description: Designed to support the NS in improving legal preparedness for disasters and crisis and to promote the use of the IDRL Guidelines in order to reduce human vulnerability.

component_responses.notes: Office of the Prime Minister of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines exempted the SVGRCS from import taxes/customs for any incoming humanitarian aid transport in 2013 floods response. Doc 12-DREF

component_details.title: Quality and accountability
component_details.description: Describes the essential elements of principled, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian action. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_responses.notes: "The SVGRCS hired a communication officer for three months to ensure that all the affected communities were included in the operational two-way feedback system; the official also focused on the operation’s beneficiary feedback mechanism and its integration with all the sectors, which was intended to guarantee that specific needs linked to gender, age, disability, ethnicity and other factors that increase vulnerability were considered. A complaint mechanism was also put in place, and accountability to beneficiaries was enhanced through the realization of a beneficiary satisfaction survey, which had a sample size of 250 families, and the provision of a feedback mechanism that allowed the affected communities to send feedback to the National Society’s headquarters."

component_details.title: RC auxiliary role, Mandate and Law
component_details.description: A constitutional reference to the role of the NS in responding to disasters and crises, which may be legislated or included/ recognized in the National Response System.

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_details.title: Scenario planning

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets

component_details.title: Business continuity

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements

Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes: "CDRTs and volunteers formed part of the Red Cross’s damage and needs assessment teams that were deployed to the affected areas immediately following the National Authority’s authorization for the 2016 floods; they were also involved in the continuous assessment process, which included focus group discussions and community consultations. Learnings: Community volunteers were invaluable members of the damage and needs assessment teams; for example, they were able to help the teams locate and access persons in locations that were not familiar to the officials, and they were also critical to the verification of information, which helped to speed up the assessments; The damage and needs assessment process ought to conduct an analysis of the special circumstances of some communities including history, ethnicity, social/economic and cultural aspects; for example, indigenous people constitute more than 80 per cent of the population of Sandy Bay, London, Magum, Overland and Owia.Doc 11-DREF"

Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_details.title: CHEMICAL, BIOLOGICAL, RADIOLOGICAL AND NUCLEAR (CBRN) EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS
MANAGEMENT OF DEAD BODIES TO FACILITATE THEIR IDENTIFICATION
NS-specific areas of intervention
component_details.description: Sector-specific or services provided by the NS in case of emergencies, it is in line with the NS mandate and legislation in country. It includes Community Based DP/DRR, Evacuation, Health in Emergencies, Epidemic and Pandemic, First aid, WASH, Food security and Livelihoods, Search and rRescue, Shelter, Management of dead bodies, RFL, Transition to recovery, and CBRN preparedness.

component_details.title: DRM Strategy
component_details.description: An outline of the overall goal that the NS seeks to achieve in its disaster and crisis response operations. The goal considers: context analysis, ongoing/regular all-hazards risk assessments: it may define the target proportion of affected population that will be reached, and a definition of the areas/sectors where a NS will usually respond during an emergency.

component_details.title: DRM Policy
component_details.description: Reflects the NS mission, RCRC principles and mandate. It acknowledges other relevant NS policies, and aligns with the government policy (where applicable), incorporating the general rules that the NS will obey in order to achieve something (i.e mandate, strategy, etc.)

component_details.title: DRM Laws, Advocacy and Dissemination
component_details.description: Designed to support the NS in improving legal preparedness for disasters and crisis and to promote the use of the IDRL Guidelines in order to reduce human vulnerability.

component_details.title: Quality and accountability
component_details.description: Describes the essential elements of principled, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian action. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_details.title: RC auxiliary role, Mandate and Law
component_details.description: A constitutional reference to the role of the NS in responding to disasters and crises, which may be legislated or included/ recognized in the National Response System.

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_details.title: Coordination with External Agencies and NGOs
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and collaboration with Non-Governmental Organization (NGO), both local and international NGOs, civil society organizations (CSOs) and United Nations agencies in country.

component_details.title: Civil Military Relations
component_details.description: Dialogue and interaction with military actors, essential to protect and promote humanitarian principles, avoid competition, minimize inconsistency and, when appropriate, pursue common goals.

component_details.title: Coordination with Movement
component_details.description: Mechanisms that facilitate the coordination with ICRC, IFRC, and PNS in-country.

component_details.title: Coordination with authorities
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and cooperation with local and national authorities. It is connected to the NS auxiliary role for humanitarian assistance.

component_details.title: Coordination with local community level responders
component_details.description: Engagement with Community Disaster Response Teams (CDRTs), through training, coordination, and the development of community disaster preparedness and response plans.

component_details.title: Cooperation with private sector
component_details.description: Mechanism that allows cooperation with private sector that often plays a strong role in response, particularly if there is impact on their staff and businesses. There is often a willingness to donate goods and services. Advance agreements help to expedite response actions.

component_details.title: Resource Mobilisation
component_details.description: A documented strategy for raising domestic funds from the government, private sector, general public and other in-country actors to support the national society’s response. This would include allocation of responsibilities, practical mechanisms for accepting funds and for being accountable on funds.

component_details.title: Staff and volunteer management
component_details.description: Well-functioning staff and volunteer management systems and practices allow for effective recruitment, supervision, support and encouragement of staff and volunteers.

component_details.title: Safety and security management
component_details.description: Addresses policy and procedures to ensure the safety of staff and volunteers. This include awareness, effective recruitment, training and management processes in place to ensure that personnel are capable of undertaking the roles demanded of them (from NS operational, management and leaders) according to the Stay Safe (IFRC) and Safer Access (ICRC). Based on safer access framework, including concepts of access, perception, identification and acceptance, and protection and violence prevention.

component_details.title: Communication in emergencies
component_details.description: Incorporates a system of public messaging to enable the NS to share timely, accurate information before, during, and after a disaster or crisis.

component_details.title: Operations Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Learning
component_details.description: The PMERL is designed to implement a results-based planning, monitoring and evaluation system that provides an evidence base of NS performance, including relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, sustainability and impact. A reliable and trusted organization is accountable, providing transparent and timely information and building systems to strengthen data collection and reporting. It is data-driven, analytical and results-based.

component_details.title: Finance and Admin policy and emergency procedures
component_details.description: Overall budgeting, accounting, treasury, assets, financial reporting and financial services operations. it also includes the efficient delivery , cost effective and timely services to the NS. Pre-approved, auditable, expedited procedures that allow for flexibility during a disaster/crisis. These must meet transparency, oversight and accountability standards. Procedures may include faster approval processes, fewer signatures, different authority levels. The Emergency Procedures are activated for a specific period of time.

component_details.title: Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
component_details.description: Refers to technologies that provide access to information through telecommunications. This includes the Internet, wireless networks, mobile phones, radios and other communication mediums.

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_details.title: CHEMICAL, BIOLOGICAL, RADIOLOGICAL AND NUCLEAR (CBRN) EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS
MANAGEMENT OF DEAD BODIES TO FACILITATE THEIR IDENTIFICATION
NS-specific areas of intervention
component_details.description: Sector-specific or services provided by the NS in case of emergencies, it is in line with the NS mandate and legislation in country. It includes Community Based DP/DRR, Evacuation, Health in Emergencies, Epidemic and Pandemic, First aid, WASH, Food security and Livelihoods, Search and rRescue, Shelter, Management of dead bodies, RFL, Transition to recovery, and CBRN preparedness.

component_details.title: Coordination with External Agencies and NGOs
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and collaboration with Non-Governmental Organization (NGO), both local and international NGOs, civil society organizations (CSOs) and United Nations agencies in country.

component_details.title: Civil Military Relations
component_details.description: Dialogue and interaction with military actors, essential to protect and promote humanitarian principles, avoid competition, minimize inconsistency and, when appropriate, pursue common goals.

component_details.title: Coordination with Movement
component_details.description: Mechanisms that facilitate the coordination with ICRC, IFRC, and PNS in-country.

component_details.title: Coordination with authorities
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and cooperation with local and national authorities. It is connected to the NS auxiliary role for humanitarian assistance.

component_details.title: Coordination with local community level responders
component_details.description: Engagement with Community Disaster Response Teams (CDRTs), through training, coordination, and the development of community disaster preparedness and response plans.

component_details.title: Cooperation with private sector
component_details.description: Mechanism that allows cooperation with private sector that often plays a strong role in response, particularly if there is impact on their staff and businesses. There is often a willingness to donate goods and services. Advance agreements help to expedite response actions.

component_details.title: RC auxiliary role, Mandate and Law
component_details.description: A constitutional reference to the role of the NS in responding to disasters and crises, which may be legislated or included/ recognized in the National Response System.

component_responses.notes: "•	GRCS auxiliary role is established by law since 1958. The Act is currently being reviewed with the National Cabinet.  •	NS mandate is reflected in policies and is well known by staff and volunteers. •	The NS promotes the IHL, especially with the Military and paramilitary agencies and coordination is done in order to promote the Laws. Trainings and sensitization are also done to those bodies by the NS through the support of ICRC.  •	The NS has a defined role in epidemic preparedness and response (Risk Communication and Community Engagement and Surveillance). The regional branches were working with the public authorities during measles, cholera, polio, COVID responses.  •	GRCS Heath Coordinator is a part of the COVID EOC led by Ministry of Health. National Technical Working Group (Public Health) for Epidemics. Health focal point also represents red cross in interagency coordination meetings chaired by Minister of Health where different agencies report activities on health and especially epidemics. •	NS role in epidemics could be defined better. "

component_details.title: DRM Strategy
component_details.description: An outline of the overall goal that the NS seeks to achieve in its disaster and crisis response operations. The goal considers: context analysis, ongoing/regular all-hazards risk assessments: it may define the target proportion of affected population that will be reached, and a definition of the areas/sectors where a NS will usually respond during an emergency.

component_responses.notes: "•	GRCS has DRM Strategy in place (2020 – 2024) and reflects the NS mandate, analysis of country context, trends, operational objectives, success indicators for the Strategic Pillars. •	It considers different specific areas of intervention, such as DM, WASH, Shelter, Livelihood, RFL, as well as cross-cutting themes.  •	There is a plan to review the Strategy every 4 years. The review will be interdepartmental which includes representation from HQ and branches as well.  •	Among ""Natural Hazards and Vulnerabilities"" , the DRM strategy identifies some public health risks such as epidemics / disease outbreaks. •	There appears to be no sectorial plans of actions linked to the DRM Strategy. •	DRM Strategy seems to also lack dissemination among staff and volunteers. "

component_details.title: DRM Policy
component_details.description: Reflects the NS mission, RCRC principles and mandate. It acknowledges other relevant NS policies, and aligns with the government policy (where applicable), incorporating the general rules that the NS will obey in order to achieve something (i.e mandate, strategy, etc.)

component_responses.notes: "•	NS doesn’t have DRM Policy; however, DRM Strategy contains some elements, which provide a framework for the NS to guide decision-making on the response approach and actions.  •	Specific GRCS overarching Policy priorities identifying for how NS shall conduct all its disaster risk management operations and programs, as well as linkages with various Movement and government frameworks still need to be outlined."

component_details.title: DRM Laws, Advocacy and Dissemination
component_details.description: Designed to support the NS in improving legal preparedness for disasters and crisis and to promote the use of the IDRL Guidelines in order to reduce human vulnerability.

component_responses.notes: "•	The Act that establishes the NS has elements of International Diplomacy but there are no specific IDRL plans in place or documents signed. •	The NS Communications Manager was trained in IHL in an emergency. •	NS doesn’t have exemptions for tax, importation custom costs etc. However, the current review of the Act (hasn’t been approved yet) includes some aspect of facilitation of International Disaster Relief and waivers of tax and duties on import of relief materials.  •	NS management understands and complies with domestic legal and policy framework relating to public health risks and public health emergencies. ICRC is supporting the NS in data policy for epidemic control to align it with the National Data Protection Commission."

component_details.title: Quality and accountability
component_details.description: Describes the essential elements of principled, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian action. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_responses.notes: "•	CEA included into the DRM Strategy as cross cutting sector and integrated to the planning of operations and programs. •	GRCS has some CEA mechanisms in place, communities are involved in the assessment, design, and implementation of activities.  •	CEA ToT has been conducted for selected HQ and regional staff, as well as volunteers. However, more subsequent training is required. •	GRCS doesn’t have HQ CEA focal point, some regional managers act as CEA FPs for the branches. •	NS doesn’t have CEA plan developed, however, some activities for improvement are incorporated to the DRM Strategy.  •	Elements of the feedback mechanism exist (suggestion boxes installed in the communities where intervention is taking place), however mechanism could be improved especially in the areas of and analyzing the received information and conducting follow-ups. •	Information on SGBV is collected through CEA mechanisms. However, the capacity of NS to respond to SGBV concerns is unclear (i.e., referral pathways).  •	NS doesn’t have PSEA Policy, however, some elements of it are included in the Code of Conduct for Staff."

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes: "•	NS doesn't have up-to-date and approved BCP for major emergency/crisis situation.  •	In the beginning of pandemic in 2019 GRCS developed COVID-19 Business Continuity Plan to ensure the organization can keep working. It was the first time that brought out the BCP idea to NS.  •	NS had experience of communication with donors to repurpose funds for unexpected or emerging needs (e.g., requesting repurposing funds of the DRR Climate Change Swiss Red Cross project)."

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_responses.notes: "•	NS doesn’t have up-to-date, approved SOPs for all specific areas of intervention and support services to respond to disasters and crises. •	When government SOPs are developed, and GRCS takes part in discussions along with other partners. •	NS provided financial and technical support to NADMO with SOPs development for 2 regions. •	Decision making flowchart which assigns decision making responsibility accordingly at each level is included to the DRM Strategy."

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_responses.notes: "•	NS does not have a pre-disaster response plan for potential hazards. NS normally develops its own response plan based on government plan and when a disaster or emergency has happened (COVID-19, Floods, Apeate Explosions, Elections) with support from partners. •	However, gender, age, disability and diversity complexities and community capacities considerations are included in the response plans.  •	Response plans include wide participation of community, staff, volunteers, governance, management, and technical inputs from IFRC where relevant. Community engagement and accountability is a high priority and embedded in all activities and planning. •	During IFRC supported operations GRCS conduct lessons learned. NS analyses the previous operation (e.g., during Apeate Explosions response)."

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes: "•	Pre-Disaster meetings are mostly held between the NS and communities and sometimes with donors. NS also participants in coordination meetings with the government and other actors. However, they mostly happen on ad hoc basis. •	Good example of pre-disaster planning are meetings that have been happening among NS and partners before the Elections.  •	NS doesn't have pre-disaster agreements with key suppliers of goods and services. The agreement with financial service provider (Fidelity bank) is signed and can be activated.  •	It does not appear that all contractors have signed the CoC, however, some elements of CoC could have been included to the contracts (to be verified by NS). •	No agreements exist in terms of import of Humanitarian aid items which poses a challenge in clearance of imported humanitarian goods. However, an agreement exists with Ministry of Foreign Affairs which helps with Visa issuance for personnel."

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_responses.notes: "•	NS has some elements of risk monitoring on national and regional levels. For example, through participating in pre-disaster meetings, information exchange with other stakeholders. It appears there is no risk monitoring focal point in NS. •	NS monitors the situation in the field and reports on major emerging, social and economic trends. In addition to primary data, the information about high-risk communities also comes from other resources (secondary data), for e.g., NADMO. NS starts with the secondary data and then goes to communities to verify it and plan and deliver an intervention. •	GRCS had experience in cross-border coordination with neighbouring countries (e.g., with Cote-d'Ivoire re Ebola response). Moreover, NS branches coordinate risk monitoring across the regions.  •	NS doesn’t have Early Warning systems established.  •	NS has experience in conducting VCAs for the communities mostly in projects’ supported locations."

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_responses.notes: "•	NS doesn't develop pre-disaster scenarios. Analysis is done when EpoA for a specific response is being developed.  •	NS hasn't developed humanitarian scenarios for high-risk areas in the country. •	NS doesn't have Contingency plans. Some regional government plans exist with the RC role mentioned for certain areas of response."

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_responses.notes: "•	The NS does not conduct risk management holistically across technical sectors and does not identify and operationalize mitigation measures (including in cases of reputational risks).  •	However, systematic finance procedure and internal control mechanism are in place for financial risks (for example, fraud and corruption prevention) •	Risk management responsibility has not been assigned to a trained and dedicated staff member.  •	The NS does not have a crisis management unit/function to manage critical incidents in a systematic way.  •	It appears that NS ensures the protection of first responders; they are only deployed after necessary training and provision of essential PPE. •	It was also noted that the NS has identified trusted sources of communication to ensure community engagement and public health messaging."

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_responses.notes: "•	This component needs improvement but participation of Ghana Red Cross in 2017 OCAC, Cash Preparedness assessments, as well as 2022 PER self-assessment process validates the commitment of GRCS towards preparedness elements.  •	It has been noted that necessary coordination exists among health and DM/Health teams for epidemic preparedness. •	Currently, there is an ongoing development of preparedness plan and budget (Standby DREF) for Flooding. •	Financial gaps for preparedness and early actions are not identified, and there is no preparedness fund available. •	In some regions there are limited prepositioned items with support of partners (e.g., shelter replenishment kits and family tents), however, not all areas are covered. Moreover, the items are not replenished. •	It was noted that having NFIs, jerry cans prepositioned in high-risk areas would also be helpful, as well as conducting a regular mapping of those areas."

"•	Considered in the DRM strategy among DRR and Livelihood areas of focus. •	Food Security approached from a community-based angle, with Mothers club including some elements. However, no systematic collection and analysis of data on food security.  •	No dedicated staff, as food interventions are not a priority for NS."

"•	Strengthening capacities of the NS in search and rescue is part of the Strategic Pillar 1 in the DRM Strategy. •	NDTRs and CDRTs are trained in Search and Rescue, but equipment is not available. •	Leadership is with the NADMO, however whereas the NS disposes of more capacities, it takes the lead. •	GRCS has ongoing collaboration with other partners, including for evacuation. "

"•	NS Interventions are community led with involvement of all the groups. However, it was noted that inclusion of marginalized groups needs to be strengthened in planning and design of programs.  •	GRCS has Community based early warning systems in projects' supported areas. The volunteers are linked up with the reports from the weather-related agencies and they feedback the communities with the information.  •	GRCS is engaged in regular awareness raising and public education on disasters and crises through Mass media, radio stations (e.g., District disaster response teams (DDRTs) participate in radio panel discussions), TV. There is also some engagement on social media, however, it could be improved.  •	The CDPRTs are trained to respond to various disasters (e.g., floods). Some trainings on Epidemics control have been conducted. However, not for all the regions."

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_responses.notes: "•	Some sectors of intervention (e.g., Shelter, Livelihoods) are missing focal points. Both at HQ and regional level staff play multiple roles (e.g., in Upper West region there is FP for Health, but also covers WASH and CVA). •	GRCS has trained staff (e.g. Head of Disaster Manager and Health Coordinator), as well as volunteers to lead the initial response. However, NS could use more trained staff, as well as equipment. •	Staff and volunteers receive trainings regarding specific areas of intervention; however, they are not regular across the country, don’t include refresher trainings and are mostly linked with the specific projects.   •	NS doesn’t have database for response materials and equipment. •	The available resources are not sufficient to cover all branches. However, in terms of warehouse stocks, materials may be shared amongst regions when needed."

"•	During Health interventions NS collaborates with Ghana Health Services department (e.g., by conducting joint multisectoral assessments and data sharing).  •	NS can identify multisectoral response needs in epidemic outbreaks (e.g., considered economic impact during epidemics. Livelihood support provided through CVA during COVID-19). •	GRCS has expertise in RCCE and surveillance (passive referral). It engages with community various groups; however, feedback and complaints mechanisms could be improved.  •	NS has experience in cross-border coordination (e.g., EVD 2015). •	GRCS doesn’t have pre-positioned items for the epidemic response (only water treatment units and mosquito nets). •	There is a lack of staff-back up, NS staff and volunteers at regional and district levels might require some capacity building (e.g., organising health in emergencies related trainings). "

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_responses.notes: "•	Elements of EWEA system exist in project supported areas. •	Main modalities include: door to door and community information centers run by communities (radio and TV). Advantage: local language + community ownership. Disadvantage: low coverage    •	No modern systems for EW/EA: text messages alerts, google forecasts.  •	Clear 2-way communication channels exist within the NS in case of emergencies, however, not always used properly. Sometimes volunteers bypass the chain of communication and contact headquarter directly without informing lead volunteer."

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_responses.notes: "•	In October 2021 GRCS engaged in CVA preparedness self-assessment to determine key action points to enhance delivery of response through CVA modality. As a result of the assessment clear PoA with timelines and budget was developed for 2022. •	NS has CBI trained and experienced staff, however, no dedicated focal point. •	NS is a part of TWG led by IFRC. •	However, there is no pre- disaster market feasibility analysis done. Most times it is conducted during a response operation in a particular region. •	Some CBI SOPs are available. One of the disadvantages of the current process is that GRCS does not get reports from the bank to track how many people received the transfer. Recommendation would be to have cash distribution report done at the end of each cash intervention for monitoring and compliance. •	GRCS has an agreement signed with Fidelity Bank (finance service provider for CVA)."

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_responses.notes: "•	GRCS doesn't have specific assessment team in place, but has some volunteers trained in data collection. NS adopts IFRC data collection templates and adjusts them based on particular disaster.  •	Data is collected through Kobo using tablets, which are usually at HQ and deployed during the disaster. Challenges include time of deployment of tablets to field, data synchronization, uploading to servers and data protection mechanisms. •	GRCS collects data disaggregated by Age, Gender, and Disability. •	Most of the assessments are done in coordination with NADMO and other partners. •	Emergency needs assessment results are cross checked and validated with community members."

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.
