component_details.description: Addresses policy and procedures to ensure the safety of staff and volunteers. This include awareness, effective recruitment, training and management processes in place to ensure that personnel are capable of undertaking the roles demanded of them (from NS operational, management and leaders) according to the Stay Safe (IFRC) and Safer Access (ICRC). Based on safer access framework, including concepts of access, perception, identification and acceptance, and protection and violence prevention.

component_details.title: Communication in emergencies
component_details.description: Incorporates a system of public messaging to enable the NS to share timely, accurate information before, during, and after a disaster or crisis.

component_details.title: Operations Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Learning
component_details.description: The PMERL is designed to implement a results-based planning, monitoring and evaluation system that provides an evidence base of NS performance, including relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, sustainability and impact. A reliable and trusted organization is accountable, providing transparent and timely information and building systems to strengthen data collection and reporting. It is data-driven, analytical and results-based.

component_details.title: Finance and Admin policy and emergency procedures
component_details.description: Overall budgeting, accounting, treasury, assets, financial reporting and financial services operations. it also includes the efficient delivery , cost effective and timely services to the NS. Pre-approved, auditable, expedited procedures that allow for flexibility during a disaster/crisis. These must meet transparency, oversight and accountability standards. Procedures may include faster approval processes, fewer signatures, different authority levels. The Emergency Procedures are activated for a specific period of time.

component_details.title: Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
component_details.description: Refers to technologies that provide access to information through telecommunications. This includes the Internet, wireless networks, mobile phones, radios and other communication mediums.

component_details.title: Resource Mobilisation
component_details.description: A documented strategy for raising domestic funds from the government, private sector, general public and other in-country actors to support the national society’s response. This would include allocation of responsibilities, practical mechanisms for accepting funds and for being accountable on funds.

component_details.title: RC auxiliary role, Mandate and Law
component_details.description: A constitutional reference to the role of the NS in responding to disasters and crises, which may be legislated or included/ recognized in the National Response System.

component_responses.notes: There is a strong auxiliary to government which is reference in the law; auxiliary role is known by most staff. The auxiliary role is mentioned in the strategic plan and in the Emergency Plan of Action (EPOA).  IHL dissemination is carried out through the communications department with volunteers at the branch and there is going advocacy work that with the national authorities.

component_details.title: DRM Strategy
component_details.description: An outline of the overall goal that the NS seeks to achieve in its disaster and crisis response operations. The goal considers: context analysis, ongoing/regular all-hazards risk assessments: it may define the target proportion of affected population that will be reached, and a definition of the areas/sectors where a NS will usually respond during an emergency.

component_responses.notes: This is a quality document which has been approved and is reference during decision making. The documents should be regularly reviewed and updated against current objectives and outputs. The DRM strategy should be linked to team structure and shared across the department. The development of the DRM strategy has been a catalyzed for the development of other department strategies.

component_details.title: DRM Policy
component_details.description: Reflects the NS mission, RCRC principles and mandate. It acknowledges other relevant NS policies, and aligns with the government policy (where applicable), incorporating the general rules that the NS will obey in order to achieve something (i.e mandate, strategy, etc.)

component_responses.notes: The policy still marked as draft although it had been approved by Executive committee since 2013. It was supposed to be reviewed in 2018.  There is not a strong link to the DM response and the policy.

component_details.title: DRM Laws, Advocacy and Dissemination
component_details.description: Designed to support the NS in improving legal preparedness for disasters and crisis and to promote the use of the IDRL Guidelines in order to reduce human vulnerability.

component_responses.notes: The DRM laws are final stages of approval (planned with the General Assembly later in 2019). The NS was active in development of  the law. Support for implementation and use of the law is planned for 2019.

component_details.title: Quality and accountability
component_details.description: Describes the essential elements of principled, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian action. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_responses.notes: The NS has a community engagement and accountability (CEA) department. Staff have been trained and service provided in coordination with other departments. There is an established feedback mechanism in place, reports are tracked, and serious incidents are escalated. There are protection practices strong, although Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS) was not reference and little is known about Sphere. The NS does has diversity in its staff and volunteers; which is typically based on geography and takes tensions and conflict into consideration.

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes: Business Continuity is planned at project level (in some cases). If a branch is affected the SSRC will approach donors to discuss support options.

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_responses.notes: There are two different SOPs documents, which have unique differences. Neither have been approved nor revised since 2014; the documents have not been disseminated. The document is insufficient for planning (i.e. does not describe roles, there are only two phases, lacks a flow chart and up-to-date organigram, etc.)  therefore affecting the SSRC response processes. There is a lack of de-escalation in the document.  This is a core component as this is linked to a number of the following components (i.e. 6,7,9,10,14,15,16,18,19,20,21,23). As such progress made this this area is likely to have a positive impact on key other elements of the response system.

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_responses.notes: There is a Movement response plan and there is a recently constitutional revision which is more gender and diversity sensitive (to be approved at the NS General Assembly in 2019). EPOAs and DREFS are aligned with standard formats, completed by SSRC and IFRCS; although can be missing key content. There is no direct recovery planning although aspects have been integrated into the Movement Response Plan for 2019.  It was unclear on how much the communities are being involved across the SSRC emergency response planning - although some good examples of community engagement were noted at a project specific level. These examples could be replicated and built on as this approach really supported the acceptance of the NS.  Could not find evidence of an exit strategy / transition out of the response phase.

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_responses.notes: There was anecdotal evidence regarding meetings with Government and various stakeholders such as participation in the cluster and task force meetings. There was no evidence of annually pre-disaster meeting and no formal capacity mapping.   The RC Lase is exempt from taxes although not clear on expediated processes therefore heavy reliance on ICRC connections.  There were some pre-suppliers’ agreements but no specific SOPS for rapid response. Cash Transfer is very costly in South Sudan and therefore no agreement in place.

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_responses.notes: While there was reference made to early warning although there was no evidence of a specific process. There is risk monitoring as part of contingency planning process with branches. The contingency plan document includes multi hazard mapping although the documents is still at draft stage and has not been share with branches.  There is capacity to gathere information from the branches and share it with HQ; good coordination system with the other parts of the movement and the authorities. There has been some training on VCAs; carrying out VCAs on project level. The Health department is technically strong and good links to the MoH.

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_responses.notes: Scenario planning is part of annual planning process, although the Contingency Planning document is still a draft form. The Contingency Plan document includes a multi-sectoral analysis, main scenarios of responses are identified, and level of response required, including limitations for each scenario. (i.e. includes information on reoccurring scenarios such as cholera). Contingency Plan document does not  include coordination mechanism with other NS from neighboring country.

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_responses.notes: While there are risk management processes currently in place, risk management is not done holistically across technical sectors. There was important recognition of the key risk factors such as reputation and financial; and there is close work and collaboration with partners.

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_responses.notes: There are no budgets for preparedness or core funding that is set aside for preparedness although in the Contingency Plan document does detail what is available and what would be needed. The SSRC, is reliant on partners in times of emergencies until the DREF and APPEAL mechanisms are initiated.  SSRC budgeting support often is provided from partners at a project level.
This component is being met through project based project and could be taken to scale by drawing on existing examples.

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_responses.notes: There is no specific mapping that has been completed; there is anecdotal and informal information which relies on relationships and networks. There is no dedicated NS focal point for intervention areas as many staff are project based and reliance on partners to augment needs. There is ad hoc awareness within the technical units regarding personnel capacity and available equipment.

Generally the activities are unidimensional; focusing mostly on hygiene promotion and mild level of epidemic prevention. Health in emergency is viewed as responsibility of DM with technical support from Health department. There was mixed information and evidence on the connections with CEA and ability to deal with rumours.  There is a strong relationship MoH including secondments and understanding of the the auxiliary role of the government. SSRC participates on task forces.  The EBOLA DREF and emergency response was strongly supported by the partners. The EBOLA response has grew out of the EOC workshop.  SSRCS has trained staff and volunteers in Safe and dignified burials (under EBOLA Preparedness), PPE available although it is unknown how expertise is retained outside of this specific EBOLA preparedness response. It is unclear whether the distinction between dead body management and SDB is well understood by all staff.  SSRC has role in epidemic response which has been defined.  The Cholera response included a Cholera treatment and WASH activities ; and was considered solid response.

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_responses.notes: There is a lack of clarity on the on detailed process of sharing early warning information and unclear whether a formal system exists; although branches appear to be monitoring the situation in their geographic areas. Some specific sectors were better placed for monitoring their risks (i.e. security in complex operating environments) The SSRC is participates in National Task Force as part of their own awareness although is it unclear the contribution of information from SSRC to the Task Force. SSRC receives information and alerts on evolving situation,  although appears to receive when already on-going and actions were tended to be more in response than in anticipation.

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_responses.notes: There has been some discussions and attempts at CTP although due to current banking situation and exchange fluctuations it would be difficult to undertake and expensive.

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_responses.notes: Emergency needs assessments are completed at department level and at branches. While training has been done, practice and experience is needed in order to take a stronger lead as there is a lack of clarity on process, templates and decision-making procedures. There are established assessments in place and NDRTs have been trained in sectoral assessments and PGIE. Although NDRT has dropped in available capacity.  Note: due to limitation of the post-operational evaluation modality of PER in 2019, there was no evidence beyond a partially filling components as the 2015 operational evaluation provided for direct observation at branches and HQ.

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_responses.notes: There is a lack of defined population and specifics is on beneficiary selection criteria is unclear; currently it is mostly support through selection by community leaders. There is no information management system and privacy policy for data of beneficiaries.

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_responses.notes: Mechanism to trigger the EOC is referenced in the Contingency Plan however it doesn’t seem to be applied during responses. There was a training provided on EOC, personnel are aware of there roles and responsibilities in case of emergency although there are no SOPs which is a major gap. There is a dedicated space for EOC which is connected to generator and has a water supply. Some equipment is not functional. (i.e. television). There is an updated contact list shared monthly.

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_responses.notes: There is sex disaggregate information although only as the head of the household (i.e.  male/female headed household). Internal communication does not appear systematic. Regular meetings are held although it was not clear on actual attendance and value added of the meetings. There were challenges with technical solutions – ie. phones work with some branches although there is little internet bandwidth so uploads are difficult and can be a time lag.  Note: IM focal point was not available during the PER so the entire process could not be verified. The control and filing could not observed although the quality of DREF, EPOAs and Reports are high.

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_responses.notes: While there is budget for lessons learned as post operations activities (i.e. as part of PMER) there does not appear to any testing either cross border or with National Authorities.

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_responses.notes: There is a lack of key documents (i.e. SOPs) that affect the functioning of the process. There is  good will from partners when ad hoc requests for response required but a lack of specific procedures.  SSRC does have has RDRT and ERU trained staff and therefore some familiarity with processes. It is likely that IFRC would likely take active role in supporting regional and international support in case of large international response. There are DMIS entries and DREF and EPOA are of good quality; although this is likely largely due to the depth of RCRC movement presence.

component_details.title: CHEMICAL, BIOLOGICAL, RADIOLOGICAL AND NUCLEAR (CBRN) EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS
MANAGEMENT OF DEAD BODIES TO FACILITATE THEIR IDENTIFICATION

component_responses.notes: While not originally part of the SSRC DM strategy; it grew out of need in the aftermath of 2016 conflict.  The DBM in 2016 created impetus for additional response areas for NS, it changed the SSRC reputation and grew community recognition.   DBM recognized by Government and SSRC has responded to several severe and complex incidents include domestic plane crash and large fire. DBM by SSRC is in the plans with Government and ICRC highly supportive with trainings, etc. Recognizing the high stress activities, PSS is available for staff.  The SSRCS is seen to be providing high level of quality level and DBM is part the strategic plan.  There was a noted difference between DBM and SDB.

RFL is within the law and actualized across country. There are additional plans to further strengthen and there is PSS support available for staff working in this area.  Good coordination with ICRC and lessons learned are being built in to the program

component_details.title: NS-specific areas of intervention
component_details.description: Sector-specific or services provided by the NS in case of emergencies, it is in line with the NS mandate and legislation in country. It includes Community Based DP/DRR, Evacuation, Health in Emergencies, Epidemic and Pandemic, First aid, WASH, Food security and Livelihoods, Search and rRescue, Shelter, Management of dead bodies, RFL, Transition to recovery, and CBRN preparedness.

component_responses.notes: First Aid and Commercial First aid is a component within Health. It is mentioned in the strategic plan. This component has been comprehensively rolled out to staff and volunteers and is part of all FA training is part of all onboarding processes. There is significant support for this within SSRC.

The technical staff are well trained,  and include ERU staff. SSRCS has access to various types of standard equipment (i.e. M40, M5, and M2 water purification units, etc.) there is cooperation with ICRC in the water treatment plant. There is knowledge about coordination with CEA and Health when to is needed. As there have been regular cholera outbreaks there has been opportunities for practice. There is coordination with Ministries at National, State and County level. There was Hygiene in Emergency flip chart with basic messaging readily available.  The WASH policy, strategy and annual planning consolidated  .

This area was mostly focused on Social mobilization with messaging is limited to hygiene promotion and awareness, it is less clinical. Activities were coordinated with MoH at National and community level. First Aid is mentioned in the SSRC Strategic plan. Staff and volunteers are aware of the program and staff and volunteers  are trained in first aid.  Volunteer award of how to refer to suspected health events to the health post and to branch. There was evidence community engagement in the CBHFA program although unclear as to whether a simulation has occurred

component_details.title: Coordination with local community level responders
component_details.description: Engagement with Community Disaster Response Teams (CDRTs), through training, coordination, and the development of community disaster preparedness and response plans.

component_responses.notes: There are some systems in place, although limited to a few branches and project driven. Where the systems do exist, it seems well structured and has led to change in operations.

component_details.title: Cooperation with private sector
component_details.description: Mechanism that allows cooperation with private sector that often plays a strong role in response, particularly if there is impact on their staff and businesses. There is often a willingness to donate goods and services. Advance agreements help to expedite response actions.

component_responses.notes: Currently not engaging actively with private sector.

component_details.title: Coordination with External Agencies and NGOs
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and collaboration with Non-Governmental Organization (NGO), both local and international NGOs, civil society organizations (CSOs) and United Nations agencies in country.

component_responses.notes: SSRC coordinates with through broader coordination mechanisms. Coordinates with some UN programs particularly POCs, WFP, and UNICEF projects. SSRCS shelter cluster role is unclear and there are no formal agreements established for coordination with other agencies.

component_details.title: Civil Military Relations
component_details.description: Dialogue and interaction with military actors, essential to protect and promote humanitarian principles, avoid competition, minimize inconsistency and, when appropriate, pursue common goals.

component_responses.notes: This was not reviewed as this is currently the primarily responsible of ICRC although SSRC joins in joint advocacy on IHL and appropriate use of the emblem. There was no use of military assets being used.

component_details.title: Coordination with Movement
component_details.description: Mechanisms that facilitate the coordination with ICRC, IFRC, and PNS in-country.

component_responses.notes: The SMCC process is working well across sectors with a need to build through all levels (HQ to field).  There is good coordination with SSRC and Movement partners in response; large response operations seem to be mostly driven by external stakeholders with SSRC as implementors.  There are some cross-border exchanges although not in DM specific areas. There are a number of plans but that need to be finalized, with long delays in approvals so action can start (i.e. Contingency plans)

component_details.title: Coordination with authorities
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and cooperation with local and national authorities. It is connected to the NS auxiliary role for humanitarian assistance.

component_responses.notes: Overall good relationship at National, state and community level with authorities; SSRC strengths are recognized by the Government. A recognition of SSRC strengths by Government partners and SSRC DM are part of agreements and have relationships with line ministries (i.e. MOHADM). The humanitarian coordination forum is in place at national and state level, SSRC is part of those mechanisms at both levels. There are regular weekly meeting and communications between all counterpart authorities are very good; it is personality based more in HQ than in field. There is sharing of equipment and assets when needed. There is application of humanitarian law and advocacy takes place; although seems more ad hoc than planned Note: As PER 2019 was a post-operational evaluation it was difficult to observe the direct relationships.

component_details.title: Staff and volunteer management
component_details.description: Well-functioning staff and volunteer management systems and practices allow for effective recruitment, supervision, support and encouragement of staff and volunteers.

component_responses.notes: The Code of Conduct is signed by all staff and volunteers as part of on-boarding process, although is not signed off an annually basis. Code of Conduct includes references to sex harassment.  There was a strong verbal expression for Duty of Care for staff and volunteers although there is no insurance in place for staff.  SSRC volunteers are regularly utilized by ICRC; this utilization may not be tracked by SSRC.  While compensation is consistent there is a risk that volunteers may become "under paid employees" as concerns have been expressed about the perdiem is needed before deployment.

component_details.title: Safety and security management
component_details.description: Addresses policy and procedures to ensure the safety of staff and volunteers. This include awareness, effective recruitment, training and management processes in place to ensure that personnel are capable of undertaking the roles demanded of them (from NS operational, management and leaders) according to the Stay Safe (IFRC) and Safer Access (ICRC). Based on safer access framework, including concepts of access, perception, identification and acceptance, and protection and violence prevention.

component_responses.notes: There is a strong movement taskforce that meet regularly. Safety and security is taken very seriously in current context. Taskforce tracks events, strong compliance for expats and staff during duty hours, after hours is personal decision for national staff. Safer Access Framework is being implemented and all staff have complete Stay Safe online training. Strong understanding of duty of care of volunteers and there is online training available for volunteers (where computer access is available). There are field movement procedures that are established (forms, Tors, Mission order, briefing process, etc.); although not always followed.  There is real concentrated efforts to consider access as part of safety and security of personnel.    Note: the rating is driven from the information on volunteer safety and security, rather than the application not the application of it as this was a post-operational

component_details.title: Communication in emergencies
component_details.description: Incorporates a system of public messaging to enable the NS to share timely, accurate information before, during, and after a disaster or crisis.

component_responses.notes: ey need to do more on integration with emergencyie

component_details.title: Operations Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Learning
component_details.description: The PMERL is designed to implement a results-based planning, monitoring and evaluation system that provides an evidence base of NS performance, including relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, sustainability and impact. A reliable and trusted organization is accountable, providing transparent and timely information and building systems to strengthen data collection and reporting. It is data-driven, analytical and results-based.

component_responses.notes: The PMER department has limited staff (currently only 3 staff) although coordinates with technical sectors The PMER Framework is currently underdevelopment. There are some standardized indicators based on Strategic Plan (ie. Indicators on first aid, number of volunteers, etc.); there is sex disaggregated data although but not age or ethnic specific data. There was a lack of clarity on DM PMER standards, although there are plans to standardize EM assessment, there is a need for more exposure to 24 and 72 hr assessment formats. There is budgeting for lesson learned exercises although due to lack of funding is often cancelled.

component_details.title: Finance and Admin policy and emergency procedures
component_details.description: Overall budgeting, accounting, treasury, assets, financial reporting and financial services operations. it also includes the efficient delivery , cost effective and timely services to the NS. Pre-approved, auditable, expedited procedures that allow for flexibility during a disaster/crisis. These must meet transparency, oversight and accountability standards. Procedures may include faster approval processes, fewer signatures, different authority levels. The Emergency Procedures are activated for a specific period of time.

component_responses.notes: Strong overall financial systems for context although no specific emergency procedures. There is not no separate fund for emergency response, and budgets often driven by partners and projects. Currently the EOC coordinator is the budget holder for emergency response.   The SG has authorized to work around taxes – there is a clearing charge.  There is an annual process for internal audit. Budgeting is done in in USD, CHF or Euro to avoid currency fluctuation.

component_details.title: Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
component_details.description: Refers to technologies that provide access to information through telecommunications. This includes the Internet, wireless networks, mobile phones, radios and other communication mediums.

component_responses.notes: SSRC staff currently use personal phones for work related business and receive recharge through finance department. Contact list exist and is updated monthly.   Radio exists in 3 branches (out of 16) and at HQ, and all vehicles have radios with their own frequency. Lack of resources is the main reason why there is no HF and VH. Call signs are assigned and trainings has been completed. Facebook and twitter accounts exist and is manage by the Communication department. SOPs for ICT are not approved.

component_details.title: Resource Mobilisation
component_details.description: A documented strategy for raising domestic funds from the government, private sector, general public and other in-country actors to support the national society’s response. This would include allocation of responsibilities, practical mechanisms for accepting funds and for being accountable on funds.

component_responses.notes: As a recently formed NS and within the current South Sudan, the SSRC relies on Partners for funding all parts of organization. It will take time to build up a solid funding base although there are plans for strategy development.

component_details.title: DRM Strategy
component_details.description: An outline of the overall goal that the NS seeks to achieve in its disaster and crisis response operations. The goal considers: context analysis, ongoing/regular all-hazards risk assessments: it may define the target proportion of affected population that will be reached, and a definition of the areas/sectors where a NS will usually respond during an emergency.

component_details.title: DRM Policy
component_details.description: Reflects the NS mission, RCRC principles and mandate. It acknowledges other relevant NS policies, and aligns with the government policy (where applicable), incorporating the general rules that the NS will obey in order to achieve something (i.e mandate, strategy, etc.)

component_details.title: DRM Laws, Advocacy and Dissemination
component_details.description: Designed to support the NS in improving legal preparedness for disasters and crisis and to promote the use of the IDRL Guidelines in order to reduce human vulnerability.

component_details.title: Quality and accountability
component_details.description: Describes the essential elements of principled, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian action. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_details.title: RC auxiliary role, Mandate and Law
component_details.description: A constitutional reference to the role of the NS in responding to disasters and crises, which may be legislated or included/ recognized in the National Response System.

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_responses.notes: (1) Needs much improvement; (2) Perhaps prioritizing this component

component_details.title: Civil Military Relations
component_details.description: Dialogue and interaction with military actors, essential to protect and promote humanitarian principles, avoid competition, minimize inconsistency and, when appropriate, pursue common goals.

component_details.title: Coordination with Movement
component_details.description: Mechanisms that facilitate the coordination with ICRC, IFRC, and PNS in-country.

component_details.title: Coordination with authorities
component_details.description: Mechanism that facilitates coordination and cooperation with local and national authorities. It is connected to the NS auxiliary role for humanitarian assistance.

component_details.title: Staff and volunteer management
component_details.description: Well-functioning staff and volunteer management systems and practices allow for effective recruitment, supervision, support and encouragement of staff and volunteers.

component_details.title: Safety and security management
component_details.description: Addresses policy and procedures to ensure the safety of staff and volunteers. This include awareness, effective recruitment, training and management processes in place to ensure that personnel are capable of undertaking the roles demanded of them (from NS operational, management and leaders) according to the Stay Safe (IFRC) and Safer Access (ICRC). Based on safer access framework, including concepts of access, perception, identification and acceptance, and protection and violence prevention.

component_details.title: Communication in emergencies
component_details.description: Incorporates a system of public messaging to enable the NS to share timely, accurate information before, during, and after a disaster or crisis.

component_details.title: Operations Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Learning
component_details.description: The PMERL is designed to implement a results-based planning, monitoring and evaluation system that provides an evidence base of NS performance, including relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, sustainability and impact. A reliable and trusted organization is accountable, providing transparent and timely information and building systems to strengthen data collection and reporting. It is data-driven, analytical and results-based.

component_details.title: Finance and Admin policy and emergency procedures
component_details.description: Overall budgeting, accounting, treasury, assets, financial reporting and financial services operations. it also includes the efficient delivery , cost effective and timely services to the NS. Pre-approved, auditable, expedited procedures that allow for flexibility during a disaster/crisis. These must meet transparency, oversight and accountability standards. Procedures may include faster approval processes, fewer signatures, different authority levels. The Emergency Procedures are activated for a specific period of time.

component_details.title: Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
component_details.description: Refers to technologies that provide access to information through telecommunications. This includes the Internet, wireless networks, mobile phones, radios and other communication mediums.

component_details.title: Resource Mobilisation
component_details.description: A documented strategy for raising domestic funds from the government, private sector, general public and other in-country actors to support the national society’s response. This would include allocation of responsibilities, practical mechanisms for accepting funds and for being accountable on funds.

component_details.title: DRM Strategy
component_details.description: An outline of the overall goal that the NS seeks to achieve in its disaster and crisis response operations. The goal considers: context analysis, ongoing/regular all-hazards risk assessments: it may define the target proportion of affected population that will be reached, and a definition of the areas/sectors where a NS will usually respond during an emergency.

component_details.title: DRM Policy
component_details.description: Reflects the NS mission, RCRC principles and mandate. It acknowledges other relevant NS policies, and aligns with the government policy (where applicable), incorporating the general rules that the NS will obey in order to achieve something (i.e mandate, strategy, etc.)

component_details.title: DRM Laws, Advocacy and Dissemination
component_details.description: Designed to support the NS in improving legal preparedness for disasters and crisis and to promote the use of the IDRL Guidelines in order to reduce human vulnerability.

component_details.title: Quality and accountability
component_details.description: Describes the essential elements of principled, accountable, and high-quality humanitarian action. The RCRC Movement provides support to the most vulnerable people in line with the Sphere and CHS standards, Code of Conduct for the RCRC Movement and NGOS in Disaster Relief and the Code for Good Partnership of the RCRC Movement, Gender & Diversity, inclusion and protection, BPI/ Do no harm, context-sensitive analysis, violence prevention, accountability to affected population and disability considerations, Community engagement and accountability (CEA).

component_details.title: RC auxiliary role, Mandate and Law
component_details.description: A constitutional reference to the role of the NS in responding to disasters and crises, which may be legislated or included/ recognized in the National Response System.

component_details.title: Hazard, Context and Risk Analysis, Monitoring and Early Warning
component_details.description: Describes how the NS monitors and maps past, present and potential hazards, disasters and crises (e.g. hazard, vulnerability assessments, gathering information from communities and government authorities) and systematically evaluates the damage that could be caused by a potential disaster/crisis, the frequency, severity of the impact, and the alert the relevant areas to scale the preparedness actions to reduce population vulnerability.

component_details.title: Scenario planning
component_details.description: A set of practical operation plans that closely mirror the generic disaster or crisis response plan but are tailored to a specific hazard type (e.g. earthquake, dengue epidemic, floods, cyclone) and a specific scenario (i.e. number of people affected, their locations and other important factors).

component_details.title: Risk management
component_details.description: A mapping of the potential risks in every area, along with its related mitigation measures. Including financial, reputational, organizational risks etc.

component_details.title: Preparedness plans and budgets
component_details.description: Plans identifying organisational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, and developing policies, procedures and activities in order to reach a level of preparedness to be able to respond effectively to a disaster or crisis. Budgets ensure that the necessary financial support is secured to allow capacities to be built and readiness maintained.

component_details.title: Business continuity
component_details.description: A strategy to counter any potential or anticipated obstacles to effective functioning of the NS, with an eye to ensuring that personnel and assets are protected and able to function in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_details.title: Emergency Response Procedures (SOPs)
component_details.description: Written guidelines that describe duties and rights of personnel, command structures, coordination with other organizations, and reporting requirements, etc. Includes detailed organogram, decision-making flow chart, and defined roles and responsibilities.

component_details.title: Response and recovery planning
component_details.description: A documented set of procedures for the disaster/crisis response and recovery process. Including use of local capacities, transition to recovery, type of activities and serivices provided during response and recovery activities and exit strategies, procedures for DREF & EA, and templates for planning, budgeting and accessing funds.

component_details.title: Pre-disaster meetings and agreements
component_details.description: A commitment to arrange meetings and agreements with Movement stakeholders and external actors to identify, plan for and address gaps for any upcoming disaster season (e.g. monsoon, floods or cyclones, or for any generic disaster/crisis event (e.g Epidemic, pandemic, confilict situations). Pre-disaster agreements should set out each partner's role in the event of a disaster/crisis.

component_details.title: Mapping of NS capacities
component_details.description: A list of the NS capacities including HR (staff, response teams and volunteers) and equipment that are available for disaster/crisis response. Teams could include branch and national response teams. This should be defined by technical speciality where relevant.

component_details.title: Early Action Mechanisms
component_details.description: Designed to translate warnings into anticipatory actions to help reduce the impact of specific disaster or crisis events. They focus on consolidating available forecasting information and putting procedures in place to ensure that a NS can act ahead of any disaster/crisis. Forecast-based financing is included within the scope of this area.

component_details.title: Cash Based Intervention (CBI)
component_details.description: An effective and flexible way, including all forms of cash and voucher-based assistance, to support people affected by emergencies, maintaining their dignity and choice, while fostering local economies. Cash should also be mainstreamed into other sectors (including Relief, shelter, livelihoods) and services (Logistics, Finance, etc.)

component_details.title: Emergency Needs Assessment
component_details.description: Assess the extent and impact of the damage caused by the disaster/crisis and the degree of vulnerability of the affected population. The first step in any emergency response, such an assessment will identify the needs that require external intervention and the gaps to be filled. It is a vital component of the programme-planning process.

component_details.title: Affected population selection
component_details.description: Identification and selection of target Affected population for interventions, using a pre-defined set of criteria based on need and vulnerability. This includes consideration of specific vulnerabilities such as disability, age and gender.

component_details.title: Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
component_details.description: A central command and control facility responsible for carrying out disaster/crisis management functions at a strategic level in an emergency situation. The common functions are to collect and analyze data; facilitate decision making that protects life and livelihoods; and disseminate those decisions to all concerned agencies and individuals. Generally located at the headquarter level of an organization.

component_details.title: Information Management (IM)
component_details.description: Ability to manage information including requesting, receiving, analyzing and disseminating as per its procedures and partner requirements (IFRC and public authorities in particular). There should be a clear digital/paper trail that documents what, when and how the NS has acted and provides key information for the development of Emergency Plan of Actions. Includes IM between levels, between departments and Situational Reports, mapping, visualisation of data, GO platform (IFRC).

component_details.title: Testing and Learning
component_details.description: Drills and Simulations allow the organization to test, identify and learn from the results of these type of exercises and incorporate learning into future preparedness and response planning.

component_details.title: Activation of regional and international support
component_details.description: Procedures for requesting and accepting regional and international support in operations, including triggering coordination mechanisms for funding, materials and human resources deployments.

component_details.title: CHEMICAL, BIOLOGICAL, RADIOLOGICAL AND NUCLEAR (CBRN) EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS
MANAGEMENT OF DEAD BODIES TO FACILITATE THEIR IDENTIFICATION

component_details.title: Resource Mobilisation

component_details.title: Staff and volunteer management

component_details.title: Safety and security management

component_details.title: Communication in emergencies
component_details.description: Incorporates a system of public messaging to enable the NS to share timely, accurate information before, during, and after a disaster or crisis.

component_details.title: Operations Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Learning

It is data-driven, analytical and results-based.
